title.zh: 卷83 列傳第48 西域
title.raw: 卷83 列傳第48 西域 Volume 83 Biographies 48: The Western Regions

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 序漢氏初開西域，有三十六國，其後分立五十五王，置校尉、都護以撫納之。

translations.literal: Preface: When the Han first opened the Western Regions, there were thirty-six states; afterward they were divided among fifty-five kings, and garrison commanders and protectors-general were installed to pacify and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: In the preface: When the Han dynasty first extended control into the Western Regions, thirty-six states were recorded; later they split into fifty-five kingdoms, and the court appointed garrison commanders and protectors-general to win them over and keep them within the fold.

sentences.zh: 王莽篡位，西域遂絕。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang usurped the throne, contact with the Western Regions was severed.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Mang seized the throne, ties with the Western Regions were cut off entirely.

sentences.zh: 至於後漢，班超所通者五十餘國，西至西海，東西四萬里，皆來朝貢，復置都護、校尉以相統攝。

translations.literal: In the Later Han, the states reached by Ban Chao numbered more than fifty, extending west to the Western Sea and four ten thousand li from east to west; all came to offer tribute, and protectors-general and garrison commanders were again installed to oversee them jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Han, Ban Chao brought more than fifty states into contact with the court, westward as far as the Western Sea and across a span of forty thousand li east to west; all sent tribute, and the dynasty again set up protectors-general and garrison commanders to hold them under central oversight.

sentences.zh: 其後或絕或通，漢朝以為勞弊中國，其官時廢時置。

translations.literal: Thereafter contact was sometimes broken and sometimes restored; the Han court regarded it as a drain that exhausted China, and these offices were abolished and re-established by turns.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward relations were intermittent; the Han government judged the enterprise too costly for the heartland, and the frontier offices were abolished and revived again and again.

sentences.zh: 暨魏、晉之後，互相吞滅，不可詳焉。

translations.literal: From the Wei and Jin onward, the states swallowed one another, and the details cannot be fully traced.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei and Jin periods, the states devoured one another in turn, and the record cannot be set out in full detail.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，遣侍御史韋節、司隸從事杜行滿使於西蕃諸國。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Yang, the attendant censor Wei Jie and the metropolitan inspector's aide Du Xingman were sent as envoys to the states of the western borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Yang, Attendant Censor Wei Jie and Metropolitan Inspector's aide Du Xingman were dispatched on missions to the western realms.

sentences.zh: 至𦋺賓，得碼碯杯；

translations.literal: At Kapiśa they obtained an agate cup;
translations.idiomatic: In Kapiśa they acquired an agate cup;

sentences.zh: 王舍城，得佛經；

translations.literal: at Rājagṛha, Buddhist scriptures;
translations.idiomatic: at Rājagṛha, Buddhist sutras;

sentences.zh: 史國，得十儛女、師子皮、火鼠毛而還。

translations.literal: at the state of Shi, ten dancing girls, lion skins, and fire-rat fur, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: and in the state of Shi, ten dancing girls, lions' pelts, and fire-rat fur, after which they returned home.

sentences.zh: 帝復令聞喜公裴矩於武威、張掖間往來以引致之。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Duke of Wenxi Pei Ju to travel back and forth between Wuwei and Zhangye to draw them in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor further charged Duke of Wenxi Pei Ju to move between Wuwei and Zhangye to entice the western states to come in.

sentences.zh: 其有君長者四十四國。

translations.literal: Of these, forty-four states had their own rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-four of these polities had rulers of their own.

sentences.zh: 矩因其使者入朝，啗以厚利，令其轉相諷諭。

translations.literal: Pei Ju, when their envoys came to court, enticed them with rich rewards and had them persuade one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: When their envoys arrived at court, Pei Ju lavished gifts on them and set them to win over the other states in succession.

sentences.zh: 大業年中，相率而來朝者三十餘國，帝因置西域校尉以應接之。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, more than thirty states came to court in succession; the emperor therefore established a garrison commander of the Western Regions to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign period, more than thirty states followed one another to the capital; the emperor accordingly appointed a Western Regions garrison commander to handle their receptions.

sentences.zh: 尋屬中國大亂，朝貢遂絕。

translations.literal: Soon afterward China fell into great disorder, and tribute missions ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the empire was convulsed by civil war, and the tribute missions stopped altogether.

sentences.zh: 然事多亡失，今所存錄者，二十國焉。

translations.literal: Yet much of the matter has been lost; what is preserved in the record now is twenty states.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the material has since been lost, however, and only twenty states remain in the account that follows.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾，本遼西鮮卑徒河涉歸子也。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun was originally the son of Shegui of the Tufa Xianbei of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun. The Tuyuhun people were descended from Shegui of the Tufa Xianbei in Liaoxi; the founder of their line was his son Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 初，涉歸有二子，庶長曰吐谷渾，少曰若洛廆。

translations.literal: At first Shegui had two sons: the elder by a concubine was named Tuyuhun, and the younger was Ruoluohe.
translations.idiomatic: Shegui had two sons: the elder, born to a secondary consort, was Tuyuhun; the younger was Ruoluohe.

sentences.zh: 涉歸死，若洛廆代統部落，是為慕容氏。

translations.literal: When Shegui died, Ruoluohe succeeded in leading the tribe; this was the Murong clan.
translations.idiomatic: After Shegui's death Ruoluohe took over the tribe, and his line became the Murong clan.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾與若洛廆不協，遂西度隴，止于甘松之南，洮水之西，南極白蘭山，數千里之地，其後遂以吐谷渾為國氏焉。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun could not get along with Ruoluohe, so he crossed Long westward and halted south of Gansong and west of the Tao River, reaching south as far as Mount Bailan—a territory of several thousand li—and later the state took Tuyuhun as its clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun quarreled with Ruoluohe, crossed the Long Mountains westward, and settled south of Gansong and west of the Tao River, extending south to Mount Bailan over a domain thousands of li across; in time the people took Tuyuhun's name as their national designation.

sentences.zh: 當魏、周之際，始稱可汗。

translations.literal: At the time of Wei and Zhou they first styled themselves khaghan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Northern Wei and Northern Zhou periods they first assumed the title of khaghan.

sentences.zh: 都伏俟城，在青海西十五里。

translations.literal: Their capital was Fuhoucheng, fifteen li west of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Their capital stood at Fuhoucheng, fifteen li west of Qinghai Lake.

sentences.zh: 有城郭而不居，隨逐水草。

translations.literal: They had walled towns but did not dwell in them, following water and pasture instead.
translations.idiomatic: They maintained walled settlements but did not live in them, moving with the seasons after grass and water.

sentences.zh: 官有王公、僕射、尚書、郎中、將軍。

translations.literal: Their offices included princes, grand tutors, masters of writing, court gentlemen, and generals.
translations.idiomatic: Their government included ranks such as prince, vice-director, secretary, gentleman-attendant, and general.

sentences.zh: 其主以皁為帽，妻戴金花。

translations.literal: The ruler wore a black hat; his wife wore golden flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The khaghan wore a black cap, and his consort wore ornaments of gold flowers.

sentences.zh: 其器械衣服略與中國同。

translations.literal: Their weapons and clothing were largely the same as China's.
translations.idiomatic: Their arms and dress were for the most part like those of the Central States.

sentences.zh: 其王公貴人多戴羃䍦，婦人裙襦辮髮，綴以珠貝。

translations.literal: Their princes and nobles mostly wore veiled caps; women wore skirts and jackets with braided hair adorned with pearls and shells.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and nobles commonly wore veiled headgear; women dressed in skirts and jackets, wore their hair in braids, and trimmed them with pearls and shell ornaments.

sentences.zh: 國無常稅。

translations.literal: The state had no fixed taxes.
translations.idiomatic: There was no regular tax system.

sentences.zh: 殺人及盜馬者死，餘坐則徵物以贖罪。

translations.literal: Murderers and horse-thieves were put to death; for other offenses goods were levied to redeem guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Killing and horse theft were capital crimes; lesser offenses were settled by payment in goods as blood-price.

sentences.zh: 風俗頗同突厥。

translations.literal: Their customs were largely like those of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs closely resembled those of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 喪有服制，葬訖而除。

translations.literal: Mourning had prescribed garments, which were cast off when the burial was finished.
translations.idiomatic: They observed mourning dress, laying it aside once the funeral was complete.

sentences.zh: 性皆貪忍。

translations.literal: By nature they were all greedy and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: They were by nature grasping and cruel.

sentences.zh: 有大麥、粟、豆。

translations.literal: They had barley, millet, and beans.
translations.idiomatic: Barley, millet, and beans grew in their lands.

sentences.zh: 青海周迴千餘里，中有小山，其俗至冬輒放牝馬於其上，言得龍種。

translations.literal: Qinghai measures more than a thousand li in circuit; within it is a small hill, and by custom every winter they turn brood mares loose upon it, saying they obtain dragon stock.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghai Lake is more than a thousand li around; a small hill rises in its midst. Each winter the people turn brood mares loose on the hill, believing that they thereby breed horses of dragon stock.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾嘗得波斯草馬，放入海，因生驄駒，能日行千里，故時稱青海驄焉。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun once obtained Persian pasture horses and turned them loose in the sea, whereupon piebald colts were born that could travel a thousand li in a day; hence they were called Qinghai piebalds.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun once acquired Persian steppe horses and pastured them by the lake; the foals born there could cover a thousand li in a day, and came to be famed as the Qinghai piebalds.

sentences.zh: 多氂牛，饒銅、鐵、朱砂。

translations.literal: Yak were numerous, and copper, iron, and cinnabar were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Yaks were plentiful, and copper, iron, and cinnabar were found in quantity.

sentences.zh: 地兼鄯善、且末。

translations.literal: Their territory included Shanshan and Qiemo.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands embraced the regions of Shanshan and Qiemo.

sentences.zh: 西北有流沙數百里，夏有熱風，傷斃行旅。

translations.literal: To the northwest was drifting sand for several hundred li; in summer there were hot winds that struck down travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred li to the northwest lay drifting sands; in summer scorching winds blew that could kill travelers on the road.

sentences.zh: 風之將至，老駝預知之，則引項而鳴，聚立，以口鼻埋沙中。

translations.literal: When the wind was about to come, old camels foreknew it, stretched their necks and cried, gathered and stood together, and buried their muzzles in the sand.
translations.idiomatic: Before a hot wind arrived, veteran camels sensed it, raised their necks and bellowed, clustered together, and buried their mouths and nostrils in the sand.

sentences.zh: 人見則知之，以氊擁蔽口鼻而避其患。

translations.literal: When people saw this they knew what was coming and wrapped felt around their mouths and noses to escape the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers who saw the camels' behavior took warning and wrapped felt over their faces to ward off the blast.

sentences.zh: 其主呂夸，在周數為邊寇，及開皇初，以兵侵弘州。

translations.literal: Their ruler Fukak, during Zhou had repeatedly raided the frontier; at the beginning of Kaihuang he invaded with troops Hong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Their ruler Fukak had raided the borders repeatedly under the Northern Zhou; early in the Kaihuang era he attacked Hong Province with an army.

sentences.zh: 高祖以弘州地曠人梗，因而廢之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, because Hong Province's land was vast and its people recalcitrant, abolished it on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu abolished Hong Province, judging its territory too broad and its population too unruly to govern easily.

sentences.zh: 遣上柱國元諧率步騎數萬擊之。

translations.literal: He sent the pillar of state Yuan Xie at the head of several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Pillar of State Yuan Xie with tens of thousands of foot and horse to strike them.

sentences.zh: 賊悉發國中兵，自曼頭至於樹敦，甲騎不絕。

translations.literal: The enemy mobilized all the troops in the state; from Mantou to Shudun, armored horsemen were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun called out their entire force, and armored cavalry stretched in an unbroken line from Mantou to Shudun.

sentences.zh: 其所署河西總管、定城王鍾利房及其太子可博汗，前後來拒戰。

translations.literal: Their appointed Hexi commander-in-chief, Prince of Dingcheng Zhong Lifang, and their heir Kebohan came in succession to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Their appointed Hexi commander, Prince of Dingcheng Zhong Lifang, and the heir Kebohan advanced one after another to meet the attack.

sentences.zh: 諧頻擊破之，俘斬甚眾。

translations.literal: Yuan Xie repeatedly defeated them and captured or slew a great host.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xie routed them again and again, taking many prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 呂夸大懼，率其親兵遠遁。

translations.literal: Fukak was greatly afraid and led his personal troops in flight far away.
translations.idiomatic: Fukak was terrified and fled into the distance with his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 其名王十三人，各率部落而降。

translations.literal: Thirteen of their titled princes each led their tribes in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen subordinate kings each brought their clans in to submit.

sentences.zh: 上以其高寧王移茲裒素得眾心，拜為大將軍，封河南王，以統降眾，自餘官賞各有差。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the Gaoning king Yizibei had long won the people's hearts, appointed him grand general and enfeoffed him as Prince of Henan to command the surrendered masses; the rest received offices and rewards in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Gaoning king Yizibei had long enjoyed the people's loyalty, the emperor made him Grand General and Prince of Henan to lead the surrendered tribes; the others received offices and rewards according to rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復來寇邊，旭州刺史皮子信出兵拒戰，為賊所敗，子信死之。

translations.literal: Before long they raided the border again; the prefect of Xu Province, Pizi Xin, marched out to resist and was defeated by the enemy; Zixin died in the fight.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they were raiding the frontier again. Prefect Pizi Xin of Xu Province marched out to meet them, was defeated, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 汶州總管梁遠以銳卒擊之，斬千餘級，奔退。

translations.literal: The Wenzhou commander Liang Yuan struck them with elite troops, beheaded more than a thousand, and they fled in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Liang Yuan of Wen Prefecture hit them with picked troops, took more than a thousand heads, and drove them back in flight.

sentences.zh: 俄而入寇廓州，州兵擊走之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they invaded Kuo Province; the provincial troops struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they crossed into Kuo Prefecture, where local troops beat them back.

sentences.zh: 呂夸在位百年，屢因喜怒廢其太子而殺之。

translations.literal: Fukak reigned for a hundred years and repeatedly, in anger or favor, deposed his heir apparent and put him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Fukak ruled for a century and more than once, in fits of anger or caprice, deposed a crown prince and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 其後太子懼見廢辱，遂謀執呂夸而降，請兵於邊吏。

translations.literal: Later the heir, fearing deposition and disgrace, plotted to seize Fukak and surrender, and asked frontier officials for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Later a crown prince, dreading deposition and humiliation, plotted to seize Fukak and defect, begging frontier officials to send troops to his aid.

sentences.zh: 秦州總管、河間王弘請將兵應之，上不許。

translations.literal: The Qinzhou commander, Prince of Hejian Hong, asked to lead troops in response; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hong of Hejian, commander of Qin Prefecture, asked to march to his support; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 太子謀洩，為其父所殺，復立其少子嵬王訶為太子。

translations.literal: The heir's plot leaked out; his father killed him and again installed his younger son, the Kui king He, as heir.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was betrayed; the father executed his son and named his younger boy, Prince Kui He, as heir instead.

sentences.zh: 疊州刺史杜粲請因其釁而討之，上又不許。

translations.literal: The Diezhou prefect Du Can asked to take advantage of the breach to campaign against them; the emperor again did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Du Can of Die Prefecture urged a punitive expedition while their house was divided; again the emperor declined.

sentences.zh: 六年，嵬王訶復懼其父誅之，謀率部落萬五千人戶將歸國，遣使詣闕，請兵迎接。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Prince Kui He again feared his father would execute him; he plotted to lead fifteen thousand households of his tribe to return to the state, sent envoys to court, and asked for troops to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Prince Kui He again feared his father would kill him. He planned to bring fifteen thousand households of his people into Sui territory and sent envoys to the capital asking for an escort.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「渾賊風俗，特異人倫，父既不慈，子復不孝。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attendants: "The Tuyuhun bandits' customs are utterly unlike human norms—the father is not kind, and the son is again unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his courtiers, "The Tuyuhun barbarians live by customs utterly unlike our norms: the father shows no kindness, and the son is no less lacking in filial duty.

sentences.zh: 朕以德訓人，何有成其惡逆也！

translations.literal: I instruct people with virtue—how could I complete their wicked rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: I teach men through virtue—how could I help them finish a wicked revolt against their own father?

sentences.zh: 吾當教之以義方耳。」

translations.literal: I should teach them the right way.
translations.idiomatic: I must teach them the proper way of righteousness instead.

sentences.zh: 乃謂使者曰：「朕受命於天，撫育四海，望使一切生人皆以仁義相向。

translations.literal: He then said to the envoys: "I received the mandate from Heaven and nurture the four seas; I hope that all living people may face one another with benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Then he addressed the envoys: "Heaven gave me the mandate to cherish the four seas, and I wish every living soul under heaven to treat others with benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 況父子天性，何得不相親愛也！

translations.literal: How much more is this so of the natural bond between father and son—how can they fail to love one another!
translations.idiomatic: How much more should father and son, bound by nature itself, cherish one another!

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾主既是嵬王之父，嵬王是吐谷渾主太子，父有不是，子須陳諫。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun ruler is Prince Kui He's father, and Prince Kui He is the Tuyuhun ruler's heir; if the father is at fault, the son must remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun khaghan is Prince Kui He's father, and Prince Kui He is his heir: when a father errs, a son must remonstrate with him.

sentences.zh: 若諫而不從，當令近臣親戚內外諷諭。

translations.literal: If he remonstrates and is not obeyed, he should have close ministers, kinsmen, and those within and without admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: If remonstrance fails, let close ministers, kinsmen, and all around them persuade him from within and without.

sentences.zh: 必不可，泣涕而道之。

translations.literal: If that still will not do, he should speak with tears streaming down.
translations.idiomatic: If even that will not move him, let the son plead with tears in his eyes.

sentences.zh: 人皆有情，必當感悟。

translations.literal: All people have feelings and will surely be moved to understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Every man has a heart; he is bound to be moved.

sentences.zh: 不可潛謀非法，受不孝之名。

translations.literal: He must not plot unlawfully in secret and bear the name of unfilial son.
translations.idiomatic: He must not plot treason in secret and earn the name of an unfilial son.

sentences.zh: 溥天之下，皆是朕臣妾，各為善事，即稱朕心。

translations.literal: Under the broad heaven all are my subjects; if each does good deeds, that accords with my heart.
translations.idiomatic: All beneath heaven are my subjects; if each of you does what is right, you will have my approval.

sentences.zh: 嵬王既有好意，欲來投朕，朕唯教嵬王為臣子之法，不可遠遣兵馬，助為惡事。」

translations.literal: Since Prince Kui He has good intentions and wishes to come submit to me, I will only teach Prince Kui He the way of a subject; I cannot send troops far away to help him do evil."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kui He means well in wishing to come to me, but I will only teach him how a son and subject should behave. I cannot dispatch an army from afar to help him commit a crime."

sentences.zh: 嵬王乃止。

translations.literal: Prince Kui He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: With that, Prince Kui He abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 八年，其名王拓拔木彌請以千餘家歸化。

translations.literal: In the eighth year their titled prince Tuoba Mumi asked to submit with more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the subordinate king Tuoba Mumi asked to bring more than a thousand households into allegiance.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「溥天之下，皆曰朕臣，雖復荒遐，未識風教，朕之撫育，俱以仁孝為本。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Under the broad heaven all are called my subjects; though they be remote and wild and know nothing of customs and teaching, my nurturing of them all takes benevolence and filial piety as its root.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "All under heaven are my subjects. Even in distant wilds where men have never known our rites, I nurture them on the foundation of benevolence and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 渾賊惛狂，妻子懷怖，並思歸化，自救危亡。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun bandit is maddened and violent; wives and children live in fear and all think of submitting to transform themselves and escape peril and death.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun ruler has grown mad and cruel; wives and children live in terror and all wish to submit in order to save themselves from ruin.

sentences.zh: 然叛夫背父，不可收納。

translations.literal: Yet a man who rebels against his husband and turns his back on his father cannot be received.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a wife who rebels against her husband and a son who turns on his father cannot simply be welcomed in.

sentences.zh: 又其本意，正自避死，若今遣拒，又復不仁。

translations.literal: Moreover their original intent was simply to escape death; if I now send them away in refusal, that would again be unkind.
translations.idiomatic: Their only aim is to escape death, however, and to turn them away now would itself be unkind.

sentences.zh: 若更有意信，但宜慰撫，任其自拔，不須出兵馬應接之。

translations.literal: If there is further sincere intent, they should only be comforted and allowed to extricate themselves on their own; there is no need to send troops and horses to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: If they are sincere, comfort them and let them come out on their own; there is no need to march troops out to escort them.

sentences.zh: 其妹夫及甥欲來，亦任其意，不勞勸誘也。」

translations.literal: If their brothers-in-law and nephews wish to come, let that too be as they wish; there is no need to labor at persuading them.
translations.idiomatic: If brothers-in-law and nephews wish to come as well, let them follow their own inclination; do not trouble yourselves to coax them.

sentences.zh: 是歲河南王移茲裒死，高祖令其弟樹歸襲統其眾。

translations.literal: That year the Prince of Henan Yizibei died; Emperor Gaozu had his younger brother Shugui succeed in leading his following.
translations.idiomatic: That year Prince of Henan Yizibei died, and Emperor Gaozu had his younger brother Shugui succeed to command his people.

sentences.zh: 平陳之後，呂夸大懼，遁逃保險，不敢為寇。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Chen, Fukak was greatly afraid, fled into hiding in strong places, and did not dare raid.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Chen, Fukak was terrified, withdrew into mountain strongholds, and no longer dared raid the borders.

sentences.zh: 十一年，呂夸卒，子伏立。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Fukak died and his son Fu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Fukak died, and his son Fu took the throne.

sentences.zh: 使其兄子無素奉表稱藩，并獻方物，請以女備後庭。

translations.literal: He sent his elder brother's son Wusu to present a memorial declaring himself a vassal, and also offered local products, asking that a daughter be placed in the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his nephew Wusu with a memorial acknowledging vassalage, together with tribute goods, and asked that a daughter be received into the imperial harem.

sentences.zh: 上謂滕王曰：「此非至誠，但急計耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the Prince of Teng: "This is not utmost sincerity, but only an expedient in urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the Prince of Teng, "This is not sincere devotion, only a desperate expedient.

sentences.zh: 乃謂無素曰：「朕知渾主欲令女事朕，若依來請，他國聞之，便當相學。

translations.literal: He then said to Wusu: "I know the Tuyuhun ruler wishes to have his daughter serve me; if I accede to this request, when other states hear of it they will imitate it.
translations.idiomatic: Then he said to Wusu, "I know your master wishes to send his daughter to me. If I grant this request, other states will hear of it and do the same.

sentences.zh: 一許一塞，是謂不平。

translations.literal: To grant one and refuse another is called unfairness.
translations.idiomatic: To accept one and refuse another would be unjust.

sentences.zh: 若並許之，又非好法。

translations.literal: If I grant all alike, that is again not a good practice.
translations.idiomatic: If I accepted them all, that would be no better a policy.

sentences.zh: 朕情存安養，欲令遂性，豈可聚斂子女以實後宮乎？」

translations.literal: My feeling is to cherish and nurture in peace and to let each fulfill his nature—how could I gather sons and daughters to fill the rear palace?"
translations.idiomatic: My wish is to let every people live in peace according to their own ways. How could I stock the harem by gathering daughters from every quarter?"

sentences.zh: 竟不許。

translations.literal: In the end he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遣刑部尚書宇文㢸撫慰之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he sent the minister of justice Yuwen Bi to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he sent Minister of Justice Yuwen Bi on a mission of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以光化公主妻伏，伏上表稱公主為天后，上不許。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he gave the Princess of Guanghua in marriage to Fu; Fu memorialized calling the princess Heavenly Empress, and the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the Princess of Guanghua was married to Fu. Fu memorialized asking to style her Heavenly Empress; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，其國大亂，國人殺伏，立其弟伏允為主。

translations.literal: The next year their state fell into great disorder; the people killed Fu and installed his younger brother Fuyun as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the realm erupted in turmoil; the people killed Fu and raised his younger brother Fuyun as ruler.

sentences.zh: 使使陳廢立之事，并謝專命之罪，且請依俗尚主，上從之。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to report the deposition and installation, and also apologized for the crime of acting on their own authority, and further asked to follow custom in marrying a princess; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys reported the deposition and enthronement, apologized for acting without imperial sanction, and again asked that a princess be given according to their custom; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是朝貢歲至，而常訪國家消息，上甚惡之。

translations.literal: From then on tribute came every year, but they also constantly inquired into the state's affairs; the emperor greatly detested this.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute arrived every year, but their envoys also kept probing court affairs, which the emperor deeply resented.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，伏允遣其子順來朝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Fuyun sent his son Shun to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Fuyun sent his son Shun to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時鐵勒犯塞，帝遣將軍馮孝慈出敦煌以禦之，孝慈戰不利。

translations.literal: At that time the Tiele raided the frontier; the emperor sent General Feng Xiaoci out from Dunhuang to resist them, and Xiaoci did not fare well in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tiele were raiding the frontier. The emperor sent General Feng Xiaoci out from Dunhuang to meet them, and Feng was defeated.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒遣使謝罪，請降，帝遣黃門侍郎裴矩慰撫之，諷令擊吐谷渾以自効。

translations.literal: The Tiele sent envoys to apologize and ask to surrender; the emperor sent the yellow-gate attendant Pei Ju to comfort them and subtly urged them to attack Tuyuhun to prove their merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele sent envoys to apologize and submit. The emperor dispatched Attendant of the Yellow Gate Pei Ju to reassure them and hinted that they should attack Tuyuhun to prove their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒許諾，即勒兵襲吐谷渾，大敗之。

translations.literal: The Tiele promised, immediately marshaled troops and raided Tuyuhun, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele agreed, marched at once against Tuyuhun, and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 伏允東走，保西平境。

translations.literal: Fuyun fled east and held the territory of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun fled eastward and held out in the Xiping region.

sentences.zh: 帝復令觀王雄出澆河、許公宇文述出西平以掩之，大破其眾。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Prince of Guan Xiong out from Jiao River and Duke of Xu Yuwen Shu out from Xiping to take them by surprise, and their forces were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Prince Xiong of Guan from the Jiao River and Duke Yuwen Shu of Xu from Xiping to take them in a pincer, and their army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 伏允遁逃，部落來降者十萬餘口，六畜三十餘萬。

translations.literal: Fuyun fled in escape; tribes that came in surrender numbered more than a hundred thousand persons, and livestock more than three hundred thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun escaped. More than a hundred thousand of his people submitted, together with more than three hundred thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 述追之急，伏允懼，南遁於山谷間。

translations.literal: Shu pressed the pursuit hard; Fuyun was afraid and fled south into the valleys and hills.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu pressed the pursuit hard. Terrified, Fuyun fled south into the mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 其故地皆空，自西平臨羌城以西，且末以東，祁連以南，雪山以北，東西四千里，南北二千里，皆為隋有。

translations.literal: Their former lands were all emptied; from Xiping's Linqiang city westward, from Qiemo eastward, from the Qilian southward, and from the Snow Mountains northward—four thousand li east to west and two thousand li north to south—all came to belong to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Their homeland lay empty. From Linqiang in Xiping west to Qiemo east, from the Qilian Mountains south to the Snow Mountains north—a span of four thousand li east to west and two thousand li north to south—all fell into Sui hands.

sentences.zh: 置郡縣鎮戍，發天下輕罪徙居之。

translations.literal: [They] established commanderies, counties, and garrison posts, and sent throughout the realm those convicted of minor offenses to be resettled there.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty established commanderies, counties, and frontier garrisons, and resettled people from across the empire who had been convicted of minor crimes.

sentences.zh: 於是留順不之遣。

translations.literal: Thereupon [they] detained Shun and did not send him away.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was then detained and not allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 伏允無以自資，率其徒數千騎客於党項。

translations.literal: Fuyun had no means to support himself, and led several thousand horsemen of his followers to sojourn among the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: With no resources to sustain himself, Fuyun led several thousand horsemen among his followers to take refuge with the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 帝立順為主，送出玉門，令統餘眾，以其大寶王尼洛周為輔。

translations.literal: The emperor installed Shun as ruler, sent him out through Yumen, ordered him to command the remaining multitude, and made his great treasure prince Niluozhou his assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor installed Shun as khan and sent him through the Jade Gate to govern the remnant tribes, appointing Niluozhou, Prince of Great Treasure, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 至西平，其部下殺洛周，順不果入而還。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiping, his subordinates killed Luozhou; Shun did not succeed in entering and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xiping, his followers killed Luozhou. Shun never entered the territory and turned back.

sentences.zh: 大業末，天下亂，伏允復其故地，屢寇河右，郡縣不能禦焉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, when the realm was in turmoil, Fuyun recovered his former lands, repeatedly raided the lands west of the Yellow River, and the commanderies and counties could not defend against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of the Daye reign, as the empire fell into chaos, Fuyun reclaimed his old lands and repeatedly raided the Hexi region until the local commanderies and counties could no longer hold him back.

sentences.zh: 党項羌者，三苗之後也。

translations.literal: The Tangut—the Tangut Qiang—are descendants of the Three Miao.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut, also called the Tangut Qiang, are said to be descendants of the Three Miao.

sentences.zh: 其種有宕昌、白狼，皆自稱獼猴種。

translations.literal: Among their tribes are Dangchang and Bailang; all call themselves the Monkey tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Among their peoples are the Dangchang and Bailang, each claiming descent from the monkey totem.

sentences.zh: 東接臨洮、西平，西拒葉護，南北數千里，處山谷間。

translations.literal: East they adjoin Lintao and Xiping; west they border Yehu; north and south for several thousand li they dwell among valleys and hills.
translations.idiomatic: They border Lintao and Xiping to the east and Yehu to the west, stretching several thousand li north and south through mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 每姓別為部落，大者五千餘騎，小者千餘騎。

translations.literal: Each surname forms a separate tribe; the large ones have more than five thousand riders, the small ones more than a thousand riders.
translations.idiomatic: Each clan forms its own tribe—large ones field more than five thousand horsemen, small ones more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 織氂牛尾及𦍩䍽毛以為屋。

translations.literal: They weave yak tails and fine wool to make their dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: They weave yak tails and fine wool into coverings for their homes.

sentences.zh: 服裘褐，披氊以為上飾。

translations.literal: They wear fur coats and coarse cloth, and drape felt as upper adornment.
translations.idiomatic: They dress in fur and coarse woolens, draping felt as their outer garment.

sentences.zh: 俗尚武力，無法令，各為生業，有戰陣則相屯聚。

translations.literal: Their custom esteems martial force; there are no laws or regulations; each pursues his own livelihood; when there is battle they gather together.
translations.idiomatic: They value martial prowess above all, keep no written laws, and live by separate trades—but when war comes, they assemble as one.

sentences.zh: 無徭賦，不相往來。

translations.literal: There are no corvée levies or taxes, and they do not visit one another.
translations.idiomatic: They pay no taxes or corvée, and seldom trade visits between tribes.

sentences.zh: 牧養氂牛、羊、猪以供食，不知稼穡。

translations.literal: They raise and pasture yaks, sheep, and pigs for food, and do not know grain cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: They raise yaks, sheep, and pigs for food and know nothing of farming.

sentences.zh: 其俗淫穢蒸報，於諸夷中最為甚。

translations.literal: Their custom is lewd and polluted with levirate marriage; among all the barbarians it is most extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs are notably licentious, including levirate unions—the most extreme among the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 無文字，但候草木以記歲時。

translations.literal: They have no writing, but only observe grasses and trees to mark the seasons of the year.
translations.idiomatic: They have no written language and mark the seasons only by watching when plants flower and wither.

sentences.zh: 三年一聚會，殺牛羊以祭天。

translations.literal: Once every three years they hold a gathering, slaughtering cattle and sheep to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years they hold a great assembly, slaughtering cattle and sheep as offerings to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 人年八十以上死者，以為令終，親戚不哭。

translations.literal: When a person who has passed eighty years dies, they consider it a good end, and relatives do not weep.
translations.idiomatic: When someone dies aged eighty or more, they take it as a life fulfilled, and kin do not mourn.

sentences.zh: 少而死者，則云大枉，共悲哭之。

translations.literal: When one dies young, they say it is a great injustice, and together grieve and weep for him.
translations.idiomatic: When the young die, they call it a grievous wrong and weep together in grief.

sentences.zh: 有琵琶、橫吹，擊缶為節。

translations.literal: They have pipa and transverse flutes, striking earthen jars for rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: They play pipa and transverse flutes, beating pottery jars to keep time.

sentences.zh: 魏、周之際，數來擾邊。

translations.literal: At the transition between Wei and Zhou, they repeatedly came to harass the border.
translations.idiomatic: During the transition from Northern Wei to Northern Zhou, they raided the frontier again and again.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相時，中原多故，因此大為寇掠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, the Central Plains had many troubles, and for this reason [the Tangut] greatly raided and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Gaozu was still Chancellor and the Central Plains were in turmoil, the Tangut stepped up their raids accordingly.

sentences.zh: 蔣公梁睿既平王謙，請因還師以討之，高祖不許。

translations.literal: Duke Jiang Liang Rui, having pacified Wang Qian, requested to take advantage of the returning army to attack them; Gaozu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: After Duke Liang Rui crushed Wang Qian's rebellion, he asked to turn his returning army against the Tangut, but Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年，有千餘家歸化。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaihuang, more than a thousand households submitted and were naturalized.
translations.idiomatic: fourth year of In of Kaihuang, more than a thousand households submitted to Sui rule.

sentences.zh: 五年，拓拔寧叢等各率眾詣旭州內附，授大將軍，其部下各有差。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Tuoba Ningcong and others each led their masses to Xu Prefecture to submit and attach themselves; they were granted the title of Grand General, and their subordinates received appointments of varying rank.
translations.idiomatic: fifth year of In of Kaihuang, Tuoba Ningcong and others led their peoples to Xu Prefecture to submit. They were made Grand Generals, and their followers received ranks according to merit.

sentences.zh: 十六年，復寇會州，詔發隴西兵以討之，大破其眾。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, they again raided Huizhou; an edict was issued to dispatch Longxi troops to attack them, and their multitude was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In 16th year of Kaihuang they raided Huizhou again. The emperor sent Longxi troops against them and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 又相率請降，願為臣妾，遣子弟入朝謝罪。

translations.literal: Again they jointly came to request surrender, wished to become subjects and servants, and sent sons and younger brothers to court to confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: They then submitted as a group, pledging fealty and sending sons and younger brothers to court to confess their crimes.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂之曰：「還語爾父兄，人生須有定居，養老長幼。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to them: "Go back and tell your fathers and elder brothers—human life requires a settled dwelling, caring for the old and raising the young.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu told them: "Go back and tell your fathers and elder brothers: a man needs a settled home in which to care for the old and raise the young.

sentences.zh: 而乃乍還乍走，不羞鄉里邪！」

translations.literal: Yet you now and then return, now and then flee—are you not ashamed before your home villages!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you flee one day and submit the next—have you no shame before your own people?

sentences.zh: 自是朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: From then on tribute to the court never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, they sent tribute without interruption.

sentences.zh: 高昌高昌國者，則漢車師前王庭也，去敦煌十三日行。

translations.literal: Gaochang—Gaochang State—is the former royal court of Han's Front Kingdom of Cheshi, thirteen days' journey from Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang—the kingdom of Gaochang—was the seat of the Han-era Front Kingdom of Cheshi, thirteen days' travel from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 其境東西三百里，南北五百里，四面多大山。

translations.literal: Its territory is three hundred li east to west and five hundred li north to south; on all four sides are many great mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory measured three hundred li east to west and five hundred li north to south, ringed on every side by tall mountains.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝遣兵西討，師旅頓敝，其中尤困者因住焉。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han sent troops west to campaign; the army was exhausted and worn, and among them those most distressed consequently settled there.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Han marched west, his army fell exhausted on campaign, and the most battered of his soldiers simply stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 其地有漢時高昌壘，故以為國號。

translations.literal: The place had a Han-era fortress called Gaochang, and for this reason it was taken as the state name.
translations.idiomatic: An old Han garrison fortress named Gaochang stood on the site, which gave the kingdom its name.

sentences.zh: 初，蠕蠕立闞伯周為高昌王。

translations.literal: Initially, the Rouran installed Kan Bozhou as King of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Rouran enthroned Kan Bozhou as king of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 伯周死，子義成立，為從兄首歸所殺。

translations.literal: Bozhou died; his son Yicheng was installed, and was killed by his older cousin's son Shougui.
translations.idiomatic: When Bozhou died, his son Yicheng succeeded—but Shougui, a cousin's son, killed him and seized power.

sentences.zh: 首歸自立為高昌王，又為高車阿伏至羅所殺。

translations.literal: Shougui installed himself as King of Gaochang, and was again killed by Avoluo of the Gök Türks.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui proclaimed himself king of Gaochang, only to be killed in turn by Avoluo of the Gök Türk confederation.

sentences.zh: 以敦煌人張孟明為主。

translations.literal: They made Zhang Mengming of Dunhuang ruler.
translations.idiomatic: They put Zhang Mengming of Dunhuang on the throne.

sentences.zh: 孟明為國人所殺，更以馬儒為王，以鞏顧、麴嘉二人為左右長史。

translations.literal: Mengming was killed by the people of the state; they then made Ma Ru king, with Gong Gu and Qu Jia as left and right chief secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: The people killed Mengming and made Ma Ru king instead, appointing Gong Gu and Qu Jia as his chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 儒又通使後魏，請內屬。

translations.literal: Ru again sent envoys to Northern Wei, requesting to be incorporated within [China].
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ru then sent envoys to Northern Wei seeking incorporation into the empire.

sentences.zh: 內屬人皆戀土，不願東遷，相與殺儒，立嘉為王。

translations.literal: The people who would have been incorporated all clung to their land and did not wish to migrate east; together they killed Ru and installed Jia as king.
translations.idiomatic: The people, unwilling to leave their homeland for an eastern resettlement, rose up and killed Ma Ru, enthroning Qu Jia in his place.

sentences.zh: 嘉字靈鳳，金城榆中人，既立，又臣于茹茹。

translations.literal: Jia, style name Lingfeng, was a native of Yuzhong in Jincheng; once installed, he again submitted to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jia, styled Lingfeng, came from Yuzhong in Jincheng. Once enthroned, he again submitted to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 及茹茹主為高車所殺，嘉又臣于高車。

translations.literal: When the Rouran ruler was killed by the Gök Türks, Jia again submitted to the Gök Türks.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran khan was killed by the Gök Türks, Qu Jia transferred his allegiance to them.

sentences.zh: 屬焉耆為挹怛所破，眾不能自統，請主於嘉。

translations.literal: At the time Karasahr was broken by the Yeda, its people could not govern themselves, and requested a ruler from Jia.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yeda destroyed Karasahr and left its people without a ruler, they asked Qu Jia to provide one.

sentences.zh: 嘉遣其第二子為焉耆王，由是始大，益為國人所服。

translations.literal: Jia sent his second son to be King of Karasahr; from this he first grew great, and was increasingly obeyed by the people of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jia sent his second son to rule Karasahr. From that point his power grew, and his own people rallied to him more firmly than ever.

sentences.zh: 嘉死，子堅立。

translations.literal: Jia died; his son Jian was installed.
translations.idiomatic: When Qu Jia died, his son Jian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 其都城周迴一千八百四十步，於坐室畫魯哀公問政於孔子之像。

translations.literal: Its capital city circled one thousand eight hundred forty paces; in the sitting hall they painted an image of Duke Ai of Lu asking Confucius about government.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's walls measured 1,840 paces around, and in the throne hall hung a painting of Duke Ai of Lu consulting Confucius on governance.

sentences.zh: 國內有城十八。

translations.literal: Within the state there are eighteen cities.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom contained eighteen walled towns.

sentences.zh: 官有令尹一人，次公二人，次左右衞，次八長史，次五將軍，次八司馬，次侍郎、校郎、主簿、從事、省事。

translations.literal: In office there is one Chief Minister, next two Dukes, next Left and Right Guards, next eight Chief Secretaries, next five Generals, next eight Majors, next Attendant Gentlemen, Collators, Chief Clerks, Staff Officers, and Administrative Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The government included a chief minister, two senior dukes, left and right guards, eight chief secretaries, five generals, eight aides-de-camp, and a full staff of attendant gentlemen, collators, chief clerks, staff officers, and administrative aides.

sentences.zh: 大事決之於王，小事長子及公評斷，不立文記。

translations.literal: Great affairs are decided by the king; small affairs are judged by the eldest son and the dukes; written records are not kept.
translations.idiomatic: The king decided major matters; the crown prince and senior dukes handled minor ones. They kept no written records of proceedings.

sentences.zh: 男子胡服，婦人裙襦，頭上作髻。

translations.literal: Men wear barbarian dress; women wear skirts and short jackets, with hair done up in topknots on the head.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore Central Asian dress; women wore skirts and jackets with their hair bound in topknots.

sentences.zh: 其風俗政令與華夏略同。

translations.literal: Their customs and government decrees are roughly the same as the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs and laws closely resembled those of China proper.

sentences.zh: 地多石磧，氣候溫暖，穀麥再熟，宜蠶，多五果。

translations.literal: The land has much rocky desert; the climate is warm; grain and wheat ripen twice; silkworms are suitable; there are many of the five fruits.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the land was stony desert, yet the climate was mild enough for two grain harvests a year, silkworms thrived, and fruit trees abounded.

sentences.zh: 有草名為羊刺，其上生蜜，而味甚佳。

translations.literal: There is a grass called yangci (sheep-thorn); on it grows honey, and the flavor is very fine.
translations.idiomatic: A plant called sheep-thorn bore a honey-like secretion of exceptional flavor.

sentences.zh: 出赤鹽如朱，白鹽如玉。

translations.literal: It produces red salt like cinnabar, white salt like jade.
translations.idiomatic: Its mines yielded red salt bright as vermilion and white salt clear as jade.

sentences.zh: 多蒲陶酒。

translations.literal: There is much grape wine.
translations.idiomatic: Grape wine was plentiful.

sentences.zh: 俗事天神，兼信佛法。

translations.literal: Their custom serves the Heavenly Spirit, and they also believe in Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: The people worshipped heavenly gods and also practiced Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 國中羊馬牧於隱僻之處，以避外寇，非貴人不知其所。

translations.literal: Within the state sheep and horses are pastured in hidden secluded places to avoid external raiders; only nobles know their locations.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep and horses were pastured in hidden valleys to evade raiders—only the nobility knew where.

sentences.zh: 北有赤石山，山北七十里有貪汗山，夏有積雪。

translations.literal: To the north is Red Stone Mountain; seventy li north of the mountain is Tanhan Mountain, which has accumulated snow in summer.
translations.idiomatic: Red Stone Mountain lay to the north; seventy li beyond it stood Mount Tanhan, still snow-capped in summer.

sentences.zh: 此山之北，鐵勒界也。

translations.literal: North of this mountain is the territory of the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: North of that range lay Tiele territory.

sentences.zh: 從武威西北，有捷路，度沙磧千餘里，四面茫然，無有蹊徑。

translations.literal: From Wuwei northwestward there is a shortcut route, crossing sandy desert for more than a thousand li; on all four sides it is boundless emptiness, with no paths or tracks.
translations.idiomatic: A shortcut ran northwest from Wuwei across more than a thousand li of desert—open emptiness in every direction, without trail or landmark.

sentences.zh: 欲往者，尋有人畜骸骨而去。

translations.literal: Those who wish to go seek human and livestock bones and follow them onward.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers had to find their way by following the bones of men and beasts left along the route.

sentences.zh: 路中或聞歌哭之聲，行人尋之，多致亡失，蓋魑魅魍魎也。

translations.literal: On the road one sometimes hears sounds of singing and weeping; travelers who seek them often meet with loss and disappearance—it is probably evil sprites and demons.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers sometimes heard phantom songs and cries along the way; those who went to investigate often vanished—work, it was said, of demons and evil spirits.

sentences.zh: 故商客往來，多取伊吾路。

translations.literal: Therefore merchant travelers going back and forth mostly take the Yiwu route.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason merchants usually took the safer road through Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 開皇十年，突厥破其四城，有二千人來歸中國。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaihuang, the Turks broke four of its cities, and two thousand persons came to submit to China.
translations.idiomatic: tenth year of In of Kaihuang the Turks captured four of its cities, and two thousand people fled to Sui territory.

sentences.zh: 堅死，子伯雅立。

translations.literal: Jian died; his son Boya was installed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian died, his son Boya succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 其大母本突厥可汗女，其父死，突厥令依其俗，伯雅不從者久之。

translations.literal: His grandmother was originally a daughter of a Türk qaghan; when his father died, the Turks ordered him to follow their custom; Boya did not comply for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother was a daughter of a Türk qaghan. After his father's death the Turks demanded he observe their levirate custom, but Boya refused for a long time.

sentences.zh: 突厥逼之，不得已而從。

translations.literal: The Turks pressed him; having no alternative, he complied.
translations.idiomatic: Under Türk pressure, he eventually gave in.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，引致諸蕃。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne and drew in the various frontier states.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he courted the submission of the frontier kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 大業四年，遣使貢獻，帝待其使甚厚。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daye, [Gaochang] sent envoys with tribute; the emperor treated their envoys very generously.
translations.idiomatic: fourth year of In of Daye, Gaochang sent tribute envoys, whom the emperor received with great honor.

sentences.zh: 明年，伯雅來朝。

translations.literal: The next year, Boya came to court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Boya came to court in person.

sentences.zh: 因從擊高麗，還尚宗女華容公主。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed in attacking Goguryeo; on return he was given in marriage to the emperor's daughter, Princess Huarong.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the campaign against Goguryeo and, on his return, was given Princess Huarong, a daughter of the imperial clan, in marriage.

sentences.zh: 八年冬歸蕃，下令國中曰：「夫經國字人，以保存為貴，寧邦緝政，以全濟為大。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighth year he returned to his frontier state and issued an order within the state saying: "For governing the state and nurturing the people, preservation is esteemed; for pacifying the realm and ordering government, complete salvation is supreme.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of eighth year of Daye he returned home and proclaimed: "To govern a nation and nurture its people, preservation is the highest virtue; to pacify the realm and maintain good order, the welfare of all is the greatest aim.

sentences.zh: 先者以國處邊荒，境連猛狄，同人無咎，被髮左衽。

translations.literal: Formerly, because the state lay in a remote border region, adjoining fierce barbarians, our people were blameless in being disheveled-haired and left-lapel dressed.
translations.idiomatic: In the past our land stood at the edge of civilization, bordered by fierce nomads, and our people wore their hair loose and their robes open to the left—as customs of the frontier required.

sentences.zh: 今大隋統御，宇宙平一，普天率土，莫不齊向。

translations.literal: Now Great Sui unifies and governs; the cosmos is peaceful and unified; throughout heaven and across the land, none fail to turn together [toward civilization].
translations.idiomatic: Now Great Sui holds sway over a unified world, and every land under heaven turns toward its civilization.

sentences.zh: 孤既沐浴和風，庶均大化，其庶人以上皆宜解辮削袵。」

translations.literal: I have already bathed in the harmonizing breeze and hope to share equally in the great transformation; all commoners and above should undo their braids and cut their lapels [to Chinese style].
translations.idiomatic: Having myself received the dynasty's civilizing influence, I wish to share that transformation with my people. All commoners and above must undo their braids and adopt the closed-lapel dress of the Central States.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而甚善之，下詔曰：「彰德嘉善，聖哲所隆，顯誠遂良，典謨貽則。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he greatly approved, and issued an edict saying: "To display virtue and promote the good is what sages and philosophers exalt; to manifest sincerity and achieve the excellent is a norm bequeathed in classical counsels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and issued an edict: "To honor virtue and reward the worthy is what the sages hold highest; to reward sincere loyalty and nurture excellence is a principle handed down in the classics.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫、弁國公、高昌王伯雅識量經遠，器懷溫裕，丹款夙著，亮節遐宣。

translations.literal: The Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Duke of Bianguo, King of Gaochang Boya—his discernment and measure extend far; his capacity and mind are warm and generous; his red loyalty was long ago evident; his bright integrity is proclaimed afar.
translations.idiomatic: Boya, King of Gaochang, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Duke of Bianguo, has long shown far-reaching judgment, a generous heart, steadfast loyalty, and shining integrity known throughout the frontier.

sentences.zh: 本自諸華，歷祚西壤，昔因多難，淪迫獯戎，數窮毀冕，翦為胡服。

translations.literal: Originally from the various Chinese [states], passing generations in the western borderlands, formerly because of many hardships he was reduced and pressed by the Xiongnu barbarians, repeatedly losing and destroying his regalia, cut off into barbarian dress.
translations.idiomatic: Though his people sprang from Chinese stock and had long ruled the western marches, repeated calamities had reduced them to barbarian dress and stripped them of civilized ceremony.

sentences.zh: 自我皇隋平一宇宙，化偃九圍，德加四表。

translations.literal: Since our august Sui pacified and unified the cosmos, civilization spread across the nine regions, and virtue extended to the four peripheries.
translations.idiomatic: Since our Sui dynasty united the world, civilization has reached the nine regions and virtue extends to the farthest borders.

sentences.zh: 伯雅踰沙忘阻，奉賮來庭，觀禮容於舊章，慕威儀之盛典。

translations.literal: Boya crossed sand and forgot barriers, brought tribute and came to court, observed ritual forms in the old regulations, and admired the majesty of the grand ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Boya crossed deserts and mountains to offer tribute at court, studied the rites of the ancestral canon, and came to cherish the solemn grandeur of imperial ceremony.

sentences.zh: 於是襲纓解辮，削衽曳裾，變夷從夏，義光前載。

translations.literal: Thereupon he inherited the tassels, undid his braids, cut his lapel and trailed his hem—transforming from barbarian to follow Xia, his righteousness shining upon former generations.
translations.idiomatic: He has put on the regalia of civilization, cut his braids, closed his robes, and turned from barbarian ways toward Chinese culture—a deed that honors his ancestors.

sentences.zh: 可賜衣冠之具，仍班製造之式。

translations.literal: He may be granted the implements of cap and robe, and the patterns for manufacture should also be distributed.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be given the full regalia of cap and gown, together with patterns by which such garments are to be made.

sentences.zh: 并遣使人部領將送。

translations.literal: And envoys shall be dispatched to lead and escort delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to deliver them and instruct his people in their use.

sentences.zh: 被以采章，復見車服之美，棄彼氊毳，還為冠帶之國。」

translations.literal: Clothed in colorful robes, he again sees the beauty of chariots and apparel; abandoning that felt and fine hair, he returns to being a land of cap and belt."
translations.idiomatic: Clad once more in brocade, he will know again the splendor of court dress and lead his kingdom back from felt and fleece to the rank of a civilized, cap-and-girdle state."

sentences.zh: 然伯雅先臣鐵勒，而鐵勒恒遣重臣在高昌國，有商胡往來者，則稅之送於鐵勒。

translations.literal: Yet Boya had previously submitted to the Tiele, and the Tiele constantly dispatched senior ministers in Gaochang State; when there were merchant barbarians going back and forth, they would tax them and send [the proceeds] to the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Boya remained a vassal of the Tiele, who kept senior officials stationed in Gaochang and levied taxes on every Sogdian merchant passing through, sending the proceeds north.

sentences.zh: 雖有此令取悅中華，然竟畏鐵勒而不敢改也。

translations.literal: Although there was this edict to please the Central States, in the end he feared the Tiele and did not dare to change.
translations.idiomatic: For all the edict's fine words meant to please China, Boya still feared the Tiele too much to enforce the change.

sentences.zh: 自是歲令使人貢其方物。

translations.literal: From this time yearly envoys were ordered to bring tribute of local products.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Gaochang sent annual tribute missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 康國者，康居之後也。

translations.literal: Kang—Kang State—is the successor of Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Kang—the state of Kang—traces its lineage to ancient Kangju.

sentences.zh: 遷徙無常，不恒故地，然自漢以來相承不絕。

translations.literal: Their migrations are without fixed pattern; they do not always remain in their old territory, yet from Han times the succession has never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The people moved often and seldom stayed in one place for long, yet their line of kings had continued unbroken since Han times.

sentences.zh: 其王本姓溫，月氏人也。

translations.literal: Their king originally bore the surname Wen; he is a Yuezhi person.
translations.idiomatic: The ruling house originally bore the surname Wen and was of Yuezhi descent.

sentences.zh: 舊居祁連山北昭武城，因被匈奴所破，西踰葱嶺，遂有其國。

translations.literal: Formerly they dwelt at Zhaowu city north of the Qilian Mountains; because they were broken by the Xiongnu, they crossed west over the Pamirs and thus possessed their state.
translations.idiomatic: They once lived at Zhaowu, north of the Qilian Mountains, until the Xiongnu broke their power and drove them west across the Pamirs to their present domain.

sentences.zh: 支庶各分王，故康國左右諸國並以昭武為姓，示不忘本也。

translations.literal: Branch lineages each separately became kings; therefore the various states to the left and right of Kang all take Zhaowu as surname, showing they do not forget their origin.
translations.idiomatic: As cadet branches split off to rule neighboring lands, the states around Kang all took Zhaowu as their surname—a reminder that they had not forgotten their origins.

sentences.zh: 王字代失畢，為人寬厚，甚得眾心。

translations.literal: The king, style name Daishibi, is a man broad and generous, greatly winning the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The present king, styled Daishibi, was a generous man who enjoyed wide popular support.

sentences.zh: 其妻突厥達度可汗女也。

translations.literal: His wife is a daughter of the Türk qaghan Datu.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was a daughter of the Türk qaghan Datu.

sentences.zh: 都於薩寶水上阿祿迪城。

translations.literal: The capital is at Aludi city on the Sabao River.
translations.idiomatic: The capital stood at Aludi on the Sabao River.

sentences.zh: 城多眾居。

translations.literal: The city has many people dwelling in it.
translations.idiomatic: The city was densely populated.

sentences.zh: 大臣三人共掌國事。

translations.literal: Three great ministers jointly manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Three senior ministers shared governance of the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 其王索髮，冠七寶金花，衣綾羅錦繡白疊。

translations.literal: Its king wears braided hair, crowns himself with a golden flower of seven treasures, and dresses in gauze, silk, brocade, embroidery, and white layered cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore his hair in braids, topped with a coronet of golden flowers set with the seven jewels, and dressed in gauze, silk, brocade, embroidered fabrics, and white layered cloth.

sentences.zh: 其妻有髻，幪以皂巾。

translations.literal: His wife wears a topknot, covered with a black cloth.
translations.idiomatic: His consort wore a topknot veiled with a black headcloth.

sentences.zh: 丈夫翦髮錦袍。

translations.literal: Men cut their hair short and wear brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: The men cropped their hair short and wore brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 名為強國，而西域諸國多歸之。

translations.literal: It is famed as a strong state, and many states of the Western Regions submit to it.
translations.idiomatic: Known as a powerful kingdom, it drew submission from many states of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 米國、史國、曹國、何國、安國、小安國、那色波國、烏那曷國、穆國皆歸附之。

translations.literal: Mi, Shi, Cao, He, An, Lesser An, Nasibo, Wunahe, and Mu states all submit and attach themselves to it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi, Shi, Cao, He, An, Lesser An, Nasibo, Wunahe, and Mu all became its tributaries.

sentences.zh: 有胡律，置於祅祠，決罰則取而斷之。

translations.literal: There is a foreign law, kept in the fire temple; when punishments are decided, it is taken out to pass judgment.
translations.idiomatic: They kept a body of foreign law in their fire temple and consulted it to decide punishments.

sentences.zh: 重罪者族，次重者死，賊盜截其足。

translations.literal: For grave crimes one punishes the whole clan; for the next grave, death; thieves and robbers have their feet cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The gravest offenses brought punishment on the whole clan; lesser capital crimes meant death; theft and robbery were punished by amputation of the feet.

sentences.zh: 人皆深目高鼻，多鬚髯。

translations.literal: The people all have deep-set eyes and high noses, with abundant beards and whiskers.
translations.idiomatic: The people were deep-eyed and high-nosed, heavily bearded.

sentences.zh: 善於商賈，諸夷交易多湊其國。

translations.literal: They are skilled at commerce; many barbarian traders gather in their state for exchange.
translations.idiomatic: They were skilled merchants, and traders from many foreign peoples flocked to their markets.

sentences.zh: 有大小鼓、琵琶、五絃、箜篌、笛。

translations.literal: They have large and small drums, pipa, five-string lutes, konghou harps, and flutes.
translations.idiomatic: Their musical instruments included large and small drums, pipa, five-string lutes, konghou harps, and flutes.

sentences.zh: 婚姻喪制與突厥同。

translations.literal: Marriage and mourning customs are the same as the Turks'.
translations.idiomatic: Their marriage customs and funeral rites matched those of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 國立祖廟，以六月祭之，諸國皆來助祭。

translations.literal: The state erects an ancestral temple and sacrifices to it in the sixth month; all the states come to assist in the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom maintained an ancestral temple, offering sacrifices in the sixth month to which rulers from neighboring states came to participate.

sentences.zh: 俗奉佛，為胡書。

translations.literal: Their custom is to revere Buddhism, and they use foreign script.
translations.idiomatic: They observed Buddhism and wrote in Sogdian script.

sentences.zh: 氣候溫，宜五穀，勤修園蔬，樹木滋茂。

translations.literal: The climate is warm, suitable for the five grains; they diligently cultivate garden vegetables, and trees grow lush.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was mild and suited to grain farming; kitchen gardens were carefully tended, and trees flourished.

sentences.zh: 出馬、駝、騾、驢、封牛、黃金、鐃沙、𧵊香、阿薩那香、瑟瑟、麖皮、氍㲣、錦疊。

translations.literal: They produce horses, camels, mules, donkeys, humped cattle, gold, naosha, zhe incense, asana incense, sese, antelope hides, qulu wool rugs, and brocade layered cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Local products included horses, camels, mules, donkeys, humped cattle, gold, naosha, zhe incense, asana incense, turquoise sese stones, antelope hides, qulu wool carpets, and layered brocades.

sentences.zh: 多蒲陶酒，富家或致千石，連年不敗。

translations.literal: There is much grape wine; wealthy families sometimes amass a thousand shi, which does not spoil for years on end.
translations.idiomatic: Grape wine was abundant; wealthy households sometimes stored as much as a thousand shi, which kept for years without spoiling.

sentences.zh: 大業中，始遣使貢方物，後遂絕焉。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they first sent envoys bearing local products in tribute; afterward the missions ceased.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era they first sent tribute missions; thereafter contact lapsed.

sentences.zh: 安國，漢時安息國也。

translations.literal: An—An State—was the Parthian state of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: An—the state of An—was the Parthian kingdom known to the Han as Anxi.

sentences.zh: 王姓昭武氏，與康國王同族，字設力登。

translations.literal: The king's surname is the Zhaowu clan, the same clan as the king of Kang; his style name is Shelideng.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Zhaowu clan, kin to the ruler of Kang, and was styled Shelideng.

sentences.zh: 妻，康國王女也。

translations.literal: His wife is a daughter of the king of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: His consort was a daughter of the king of Kang.

sentences.zh: 都在那密水南，城有五重，環以流水。

translations.literal: The capital is south of the Namih River; the city has five layers of walls, encircled by flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: The capital stood south of the Namih River, in a city of five concentric walls ringed by canals.

sentences.zh: 宮殿皆為平頭。

translations.literal: The palaces are all flat-roofed.
translations.idiomatic: The palace buildings all had flat roofs.

sentences.zh: 王坐金駝座，高七八尺。

translations.literal: The king sits on a golden camel throne, seven or eight chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The king sat on a golden camel throne seven or eight chi tall.

sentences.zh: 每聽政，與妻相對，大臣三人評理國事。

translations.literal: Whenever he holds court, he sits facing his wife, and three great ministers adjudicate state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When holding court he sat facing his consort while three senior ministers deliberated on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 風俗同於康國，唯妻其姊妹，及母子遞相禽獸，此為異也。

translations.literal: Customs are the same as Kang; only that they marry their sisters, and mothers and sons successively treat one another as beasts—this is what differs.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs largely matched those of Kang, save that men married their sisters and mothers and sons successively engaged in illicit sexual relations with one another—these were the notable differences.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位之後，遣司隸從事杜行滿使於西域，至其國，得五色鹽而返。

translations.literal: After Emperor Yang took the throne, he dispatched Supervisory Censor aide Du Xingman on a mission to the Western Regions; arriving at this state, he obtained five-colored salt and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang's accession he sent Supervisory Censor aide Du Xingman to the Western Regions; reaching An, Du acquired five-colored salt and returned home.

sentences.zh: 國之西百餘里有畢國，可千餘家。

translations.literal: West of the state, over a hundred li away, is Bi State, with perhaps a thousand or more households.
translations.idiomatic: Some hundred li west lay Bi, a settlement of roughly a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 其國無君長，安國統之。

translations.literal: That state has no lord or chief; An governs it.
translations.idiomatic: It had no ruler of its own and was administered by An.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，遣使貢獻，後遂絕焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye they sent envoys with tribute; afterward contact ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye it sent a tribute mission; thereafter no further embassies came.

sentences.zh: 石國，居於藥殺水，都城方十餘里。

translations.literal: Shi—Shi State—lies on the Yash River; its capital city is about ten-odd li square.
translations.idiomatic: Shi—the state of Shi—stood on the Yash River, its capital measuring roughly ten li square.

sentences.zh: 其王姓石，名涅。

translations.literal: Its king's surname is Shi; his personal name is Nie.
translations.idiomatic: The king bore the surname Shi and the personal name Nie.

sentences.zh: 國城之東南立屋，置座於中，正月六日、七月十五日以王父母燒餘之骨，金甕盛之，置于牀上，巡遶而行，散以花香雜果，王率臣下設祭焉。

translations.literal: Southeast of the state city a house is erected, with a seat placed inside; on the sixth day of the first month and the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the burnt bones remaining from the king's forebears are placed in golden urns, set on a couch, and carried around in procession, scattering flowers, incense, and assorted fruits; the king leads his ministers in making sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the capital they built a hall with a ceremonial seat at its center. On the sixth day of the first month and the fifteenth of the seventh, the cremated remains of royal ancestors were placed in golden urns, set on a platform, and carried in procession while flowers, incense, and fruit were scattered; the king and his court then performed sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 禮終，王與夫人出就別帳，臣下以次列坐，享宴而罷。

translations.literal: When the rites are finished, the king and the lady go out to a separate tent; the ministers sit in order below, feasting before dispersing.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended, the king and queen withdrew to a separate pavilion while officials took their seats in rank order for a feast before dispersing.

sentences.zh: 有粟麥，多良馬。

translations.literal: They have millet and wheat, and many fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: They raised millet and wheat and bred many fine horses.

sentences.zh: 其俗善戰，曾貳於突厥，射匱可汗興兵滅之，令特勤甸職攝其國事。

translations.literal: Their custom is to be skilled in warfare; they once sided with the Turks; Qaghan Shekui raised troops and destroyed them, appointing Tegin Dianzhi to administer their state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They were a warlike people who had once rebelled against the Turks; Qaghan Shekui marched against them, overthrew the kingdom, and installed Tegin Dianzhi to govern in its place.

sentences.zh: 南去鏺汗六百里，東南去瓜州六千里。

translations.literal: Six hundred li south to Kapul; six thousand li southeast to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It lay six hundred li south of Kapul and six thousand li southeast of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 甸職以大業五年遣使朝貢，其後不復至。

translations.literal: Dianzhi in the fifth year of Daye sent envoys to court with tribute; thereafter he did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: Dianzhi sent a tribute mission in the fifth year of Daye; no further embassies followed.

sentences.zh: 女國，在葱嶺之南，其國代以女為王。

translations.literal: Women State—Women State—lies south of the Pamirs; that state generation after generation takes a woman as king.
translations.idiomatic: The Women's Kingdom—the state of Women—lay south of the Pamirs, where rulership passed from queen to queen in every generation.

sentences.zh: 王姓蘇毗，字末羯，在位二十年。

translations.literal: The queen's surname is Subi; her style name is Mojie; she has reigned twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: The reigning queen belonged to the Subi clan, was styled Mojie, and had held the throne for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 女王之夫，號曰金聚，不知政事。

translations.literal: The queen's husband is titled Gold Gathering; he does not know governance.
translations.idiomatic: The queen's consort, titled Gold Gathering, took no part in government.

sentences.zh: 國內丈夫唯以征伐為務。

translations.literal: Within the state, men devote themselves solely to military campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: The men of the kingdom concerned themselves only with warfare.

sentences.zh: 山上為城，方五六里，人有萬家。

translations.literal: On a mountain they build their city, five or six li square; the people number ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Their capital stood on a mountainside, five or six li square, with a population of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 王居九層之樓，侍女數百人，五日一聽朝。

translations.literal: The queen dwells in a nine-story tower; several hundred attending women; she holds court once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: The queen lived in a nine-story tower attended by several hundred serving women and held court every five days.

sentences.zh: 復有小女王，共知國政。

translations.literal: Moreover there is a lesser queen who jointly handles state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary queen shared in the governance of the realm.

sentences.zh: 其俗貴婦人，輕丈夫，而性不妬忌。

translations.literal: Their custom esteems women and despises men, yet in nature they are not jealous.
translations.idiomatic: Women held honor while men were held lightly, yet jealousy was unknown among them.

sentences.zh: 男女皆以彩色塗面，一日之中，或數度變改之。

translations.literal: Men and women all paint their faces with colors; within a single day they may change it several times.
translations.idiomatic: Both men and women painted their faces in bright colors, changing the design several times within a single day.

sentences.zh: 人皆被髮，以皮為鞋，課稅無常。

translations.literal: The people all wear their hair loose; they use hide for shoes; taxation has no fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: They wore their hair loose, shod themselves in leather, and paid taxes on no fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 氣候多寒，以射獵為業。

translations.literal: The climate is mostly cold; they take hunting as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was harsh and cold, and hunting was their chief livelihood.

sentences.zh: 出鍮石、朱砂、麝香、氂牛、駿馬、蜀馬。

translations.literal: They produce brass stone, cinnabar, musk, yak, swift horses, and Shu horses.
translations.idiomatic: Local products included brass ore, cinnabar, musk, yaks, swift horses, and horses from Shu.

sentences.zh: 尤多鹽，恒將鹽向天竺興販，其利數倍。

translations.literal: Salt is especially abundant; they constantly carry salt to trade in India, with profits several times over.
translations.idiomatic: Salt was especially abundant; merchants regularly carried it to India for trade at several times the usual profit.

sentences.zh: 亦數與天竺及党項戰爭。

translations.literal: They also frequently war with India and the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: They also fought repeatedly with India and the Tangut peoples.

sentences.zh: 其女王死，國中則厚斂金錢，求死者族中之賢女二人，一為女王，次為小王。

translations.literal: When their queen dies, within the state they heavily levy gold and money, seeking two worthy women from the deceased's clan—one becomes queen, the next becomes lesser queen.
translations.idiomatic: When a queen died, the realm levied heavy contributions in gold and silver to select two worthy women from the deceased queen's clan—one as queen, the other as secondary queen.

sentences.zh: 貴人死，剝取皮，以金屑和骨肉置於瓶內而埋之。

translations.literal: When a noble dies, the skin is flayed off; gold filings are mixed with flesh and bone, placed in a vessel, and buried.
translations.idiomatic: When a noble died, the skin was removed, the flesh and bones mixed with gold dust, placed in a jar, and buried.

sentences.zh: 經一年，又以其皮內於鐵器埋之。

translations.literal: After one year passes, the skin is again placed inside an iron vessel and buried.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the skin was placed in an iron container and buried separately.

sentences.zh: 俗事阿修羅神，又有樹神，歲初以人祭，或用獼猴。

translations.literal: Their custom venerates the Asura god; there is also a tree god; at the year's start they sacrifice humans, or sometimes macaques.
translations.idiomatic: They worshipped the Asura deity and a tree spirit, offering human sacrifices—or occasionally macaques—at the year's opening.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，入山祝之，有一鳥如雌雉，來集掌上，破其腹而視之，有粟則年豐，沙石則有災，謂之鳥卜。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice is finished, they enter the mountains to pray; a bird like a hen pheasant comes to alight on the palm; they break open its belly and look inside—if there is millet, the year will be abundant; if sand and stone, there will be disaster; this is called bird divination.
translations.idiomatic: After the sacrifice they withdrew into the mountains to pray until a hen-pheasant-like bird alighted on someone's palm; they then opened its belly—millet within foretold a bountiful year, sand and gravel foretold disaster. This was called bird divination.

sentences.zh: 開皇六年，遣使朝貢，其後遂絕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaihuang they sent envoys to court with tribute; thereafter contact ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaihuang a tribute mission was sent; thereafter no further embassies came.

sentences.zh: 焉耆國，都白山之南七十里，漢時舊國也。

translations.literal: Yanqi—Yanqi State—has its capital seventy li south of White Mountain; it is an old state from Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi—the state of Yanqi—had its capital seventy li south of White Mountain and was an ancient kingdom already known to the Han.

sentences.zh: 其王姓龍，字突騎。

translations.literal: Its king's surname is Long; his style name is Tuqi.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Long clan and was styled Tuqi.

sentences.zh: 都城方二里。

translations.literal: The capital city is two li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured two li square.

sentences.zh: 國內有九城，勝兵千餘人。

translations.literal: Within the state there are nine cities; battle-ready troops number over a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom held nine walled towns and could field a little over a thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 國無綱維。

translations.literal: The state has no laws or governance.
