translations.idiomatic: The realm had no effective legal order.

sentences.zh: 其俗奉佛書，類婆羅門。

translations.literal: Their custom reveres Buddhist scriptures, resembling Brahmins.
translations.idiomatic: They followed Buddhist scripture in ways resembling Brahmanical practice.

sentences.zh: 婚姻之禮有同華夏。

translations.literal: The rites of marriage are the same as the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Their marriage rites resembled those of the Central States.

sentences.zh: 死者焚之，持服七日。

translations.literal: The dead are cremated; mourning garments are worn for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were cremated and mourners wore funeral garb for seven days.

sentences.zh: 男子剪髮。

translations.literal: Men cut their hair short.
translations.idiomatic: The men cropped their hair short.

sentences.zh: 有魚鹽蒲葦之利。

translations.literal: They have the advantages of fish, salt, and rushes.
translations.idiomatic: They profited from fisheries, salt, and reed marshes.

sentences.zh: 東去高昌九百里，西去龜茲九百里，皆沙磧。

translations.literal: Nine hundred li east to Gaochang, nine hundred li west to Kucha—all sandy desert.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang lay nine hundred li to the east and Kucha nine hundred li to the west, all across sandy desert.

sentences.zh: 東南去瓜州二千二百里。

translations.literal: Two thousand two hundred li southeast to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guazhou stood two thousand two hundred li to the southeast.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they sent envoys bearing local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it sent tribute missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 龜茲國，都白山之南百七十里，漢時舊國也。

translations.literal: Kucha—Kucha State—has its capital one hundred seventy li south of White Mountain; it is an old state from Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha—the state of Kucha—had its capital one hundred seventy li south of White Mountain and was an ancient kingdom known to the Han.

sentences.zh: 其王姓白，字蘇尼咥。

translations.literal: Its king's surname is Bai; his style name is Sunie.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Bai clan and was styled Sunie.

sentences.zh: 都城方六里。

translations.literal: The capital city is six li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured six li square.

sentences.zh: 勝兵者數千。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: It could field several thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 俗殺人者死，劫賊斷其一臂，并刖一足。

translations.literal: Custom: murderers are put to death; robbers have one arm cut off and one foot amputated as well.
translations.idiomatic: Murderers were executed; robbers lost an arm and had a foot amputated as well.

sentences.zh: 俗與焉耆同。

translations.literal: Customs are the same as Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs matched those of Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 王頭繫綵帶，垂之於後，坐金師子座。

translations.literal: The king ties a colored ribbon on his head, letting it hang behind; he sits on a golden lion throne.
translations.idiomatic: The king bound a colored ribbon around his head with the ends trailing behind and sat upon a golden lion throne.

sentences.zh: 土多稻、粟、菽、麥，饒銅、鐵、鉛、麖皮、氍㲣、鐃沙、鹽綠、雌黃、胡粉、安息香、良馬、封牛。

translations.literal: The land produces much rice, millet, beans, and wheat, and is rich in copper, iron, lead, antelope hides, qulu wool rugs, naosha, salt-green, orpiment, foreign powder, benzoin, fine horses, and humped cattle.
translations.idiomatic: The land yielded rice, millet, beans, and wheat in abundance, along with copper, iron, lead, antelope hides, qulu wool carpets, naosha, salt-green minerals, orpiment, lead white powder, benzoin, fine horses, and humped cattle.

sentences.zh: 東去焉耆九百里，南去于闐千四百里，西去疏勒千五百里，西北去突厥牙六百餘里，東南去瓜州三千一百里。

translations.literal: Nine hundred li east to Yanqi, one thousand four hundred li south to Khotan, one thousand five hundred li west to Kashgar, over six hundred li northwest to the Türk royal encampment, three thousand one hundred li southeast to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi lay nine hundred li to the east, Khotan fourteen hundred li south, Kashgar fifteen hundred li west, the Türk royal camp a little over six hundred li northwest, and Guazhou three thousand one hundred li southeast.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they sent envoys bearing local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it sent tribute missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 疏勒國，都白山南百餘里，漢時舊國也。

translations.literal: Shule—Shule State—has its capital over a hundred li south of White Mountain; it is an old state from Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar—the state of Shule—had its capital a little over a hundred li south of White Mountain and was an ancient kingdom known to the Han.

sentences.zh: 其王字阿彌厥，手足皆六指。

translations.literal: Its king's style name is Amijue; hands and feet all have six fingers.
translations.idiomatic: The king was styled Amijue and was born with six fingers on each hand and foot.

sentences.zh: 產子非六指者，即不育。

translations.literal: Children born without six fingers are not reared.
translations.idiomatic: Infants born without six fingers were not permitted to live.

sentences.zh: 都城方五里。

translations.literal: The capital city is five li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured five li square.

sentences.zh: 國內有大城十二，小城數十，勝兵者二千人。

translations.literal: Within the state there are twelve great cities and several tens of small cities; battle-ready troops number two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom held twelve major walled towns and several dozen smaller ones and could field two thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 王戴金師子冠。

translations.literal: The king wears a golden lion crown.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a golden lion crown.

sentences.zh: 土多稻、粟、麻、麥、銅、鐵、錦、雌黃，每歲常供送於突厥。

translations.literal: The land has much rice, millet, hemp, wheat, copper, iron, brocade, and orpiment; every year these are regularly supplied and sent to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: The land produced rice, millet, hemp, wheat, copper, iron, brocade, and orpiment, which were delivered annually as tribute to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 南有黃河，西帶葱嶺，東去龜茲千五百里，西去鏺汗國千里，南去朱俱波八九百里，東北去突厥牙千餘里，東南去瓜州四千六百里。

translations.literal: To the south is the Yellow River; to the west it borders the Pamirs; one thousand five hundred li east to Kucha, one thousand li west to Kapul, eight or nine hundred li south to Zhujubo, over one thousand li northeast to the Türk royal encampment, four thousand six hundred li southeast to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River lay to the south and the Pamirs marked its western border; Kucha stood fifteen hundred li east, Kapul a thousand li west, Zhujubo eight or nine hundred li south, the Türk royal camp over a thousand li northeast, and Guazhou forty-six hundred li southeast.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they sent envoys bearing local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it sent tribute missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 于闐國，都葱嶺之北二百餘里。

translations.literal: Khotan—Khotan State—has its capital over two hundred li north of the Pamirs.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan—the state of Khotan—had its capital a little over two hundred li north of the Pamirs.

sentences.zh: 其王姓王，字卑示閉練。

translations.literal: Its king's surname is Wang; his style name is Beishibilian.
translations.idiomatic: The king bore the surname Wang and was styled Beishibilian.

sentences.zh: 都城方八九里。

translations.literal: The capital city is eight or nine li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured eight or nine li square.

sentences.zh: 國中大城有五，小城數十，勝兵者數千人。

translations.literal: Within the state there are five great cities and several tens of small cities; battle-ready troops number several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom held five major walled towns and several dozen smaller ones and could field several thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 俗奉佛，尤多僧尼，王每持齋戒。

translations.literal: Their custom is to revere Buddhism; monks and nuns are especially numerous; the king regularly observes fasting precepts.
translations.idiomatic: They were devout Buddhists with an especially large monastic community; the king himself regularly kept the fasting precepts.

sentences.zh: 城南五十里有贊摩寺者，云是羅漢比丘比盧旃所造，石上有辟支佛徒跣之跡。

translations.literal: Fifty li south of the city is Zanmo Temple, said to have been built by the arhat monk Piludana; on the stone are the barefoot tracks of a pratyekabuddha.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li south of the capital stood Zanmo Temple, said to have been founded by the arhat Piludana; on its stones were the barefoot footprints of a pratyekabuddha.

sentences.zh: 于闐西五百里有比摩寺，云是老子化胡成佛之所。

translations.literal: Five hundred li west of Khotan is Bimo Temple, said to be the place where Laozi transformed the barbarians and became Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li west of Khotan stood Bimo Temple, held to be the site where Laozi transformed the barbarians and attained Buddhahood.

sentences.zh: 俗無禮義，多賊盜淫縱。

translations.literal: Their customs lack ritual propriety; there are many thieves, robbers, and licentious excess.
translations.idiomatic: Propriety was little observed; theft, robbery, and sexual license were common.

sentences.zh: 王錦帽，金鼠冠，妻戴金花。

translations.literal: The king wears a brocade cap and a golden rat crown; his wife wears golden flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a brocade cap and a golden rat crown; his consort wore ornaments of golden flowers.

sentences.zh: 其王髮不令人見。

translations.literal: The king's hair is not permitted to be seen by others.
translations.idiomatic: No one was permitted to see the king's hair.

sentences.zh: 俗云，若見王髮，年必儉。

translations.literal: Custom says that if one sees the king's hair, the year will surely be lean.
translations.idiomatic: Popular belief held that anyone who glimpsed the king's hair would bring famine upon the year.

sentences.zh: 土多麻、麥、粟、稻、五果，多園林，山多美玉。

translations.literal: The soil has much hemp, wheat, millet, rice, and the five fruits; there are many orchards and gardens, and the mountains have much fine jade.
translations.idiomatic: The land yielded hemp, wheat, millet, rice, and orchard fruits; gardens were plentiful, and the mountains held fine jade.

sentences.zh: 東去鄯善千五百里，南去女國三千里，西去朱俱波千里，北去龜茲千四百里，東北去瓜州二千八百里。

translations.literal: East to Shanshan is one thousand five hundred li, south to the Women's State three thousand li, west to Zhujubo one thousand li, north to Kucha one thousand four hundred li, northeast to Guazhou two thousand eight hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Shanshan lay fifteen hundred li to the east, the Women's Kingdom three thousand li south, Zhujubo a thousand li west, Kucha fourteen hundred li north, and Guazhou twenty-eight hundred li northeast.

sentences.zh: 大業中，頻遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they repeatedly sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era Khotan repeatedly sent tribute missions to the capital.

sentences.zh: 鏺汗國，都葱嶺之西五百餘里，古渠搜國也。

translations.literal: Kapul—Kapul State—has its capital over five hundred li west of the Pamirs; it is the ancient state of Qusou.
translations.idiomatic: Kapul—the state of Kapul—had its capital a little over five hundred li west of the Pamirs, on the site of the ancient kingdom of Qusou.

sentences.zh: 王姓昭武，字阿利柒。

translations.literal: The king's surname is Zhaowu; his style name is Aoliqi.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Zhaowu clan and was styled Aoliqi.

sentences.zh: 都城方四里。

translations.literal: The capital city is four li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured four li square.

sentences.zh: 勝兵數千人。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: It could field several thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 王坐金羊牀，妻戴金花。

translations.literal: The king sits on a golden ram couch; his wife wears golden flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The king sat upon a golden ram throne, and his consort wore ornaments of golden flowers.

sentences.zh: 俗多朱砂、金、鐵。

translations.literal: Their land commonly has much cinnabar, gold, and iron.
translations.idiomatic: The land produced cinnabar, gold, and iron in abundance.

sentences.zh: 東去疏勒千里，西去蘇對沙那國五百里，西北去石國五百里，東北去突厥牙二千餘里，東去瓜州五千五百里。

translations.literal: East to Shule is one thousand li, west to Suduishana State five hundred li, northwest to Shi State five hundred li, northeast to the Türk royal camp over two thousand li, east to Guazhou five thousand five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar lay a thousand li east, Suduishana five hundred li west, Shi five hundred li northwest, the Türk royal camp over two thousand li northeast, and Guazhou fifty-five hundred li east.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they sent envoys bearing local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it sent tribute missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 吐火羅國，都葱嶺西五百里，與挹怛雜居。

translations.literal: Tokhara—Tokhara State—has its capital five hundred li west of the Pamirs and lives mingled with the Yeda.
translations.idiomatic: Tokhara—the state of Tokhara—had its capital five hundred li west of the Pamirs and lived mingled with the Yeda.

sentences.zh: 都城方二里。

translations.literal: The capital city is two li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured two li square.

sentences.zh: 勝兵者十萬人，皆習戰。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number one hundred thousand men, all practiced in warfare.
translations.idiomatic: It could field a hundred thousand fighting men, all trained for war.

sentences.zh: 其俗奉佛。

translations.literal: Their custom is to revere Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: They were devout Buddhists.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同一妻，迭寢焉，每一人入房，戶外挂其衣以為志。

translations.literal: Brothers share one wife, taking turns in sleeping with her; whenever one man enters the room, he hangs his garment outside the door as a sign.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers shared one wife, taking turns with her; when one entered the bedchamber, he hung his garment outside the door as a sign.

sentences.zh: 生子屬其長兄。

translations.literal: Children born belong to the eldest brother.
translations.idiomatic: Any children born belonged to the eldest brother.

sentences.zh: 其山穴中有神馬，每歲牧牝馬於穴所，必產名駒。

translations.literal: In a mountain cave there is a divine horse; each year mares are pastured at the cave site, and they unfailingly produce famous foals.
translations.idiomatic: A sacred stallion dwelt in a mountain cave there; each year mares were pastured at the cave and unfailingly bore famous foals.

sentences.zh: 南去漕國千七百里，東去瓜州五千八百里。

translations.literal: South to Caoguo is one thousand seven hundred li, east to Guazhou five thousand eight hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Kapiśa lay seventeen hundred li south, and Guazhou fifty-eight hundred li east.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it sent tribute missions to the capital.

sentences.zh: 挹怛挹怛國，都烏滸水南二百餘里，大月氏之種類也。

translations.literal: Yeda—Yeda State—has its capital over two hundred li south of the Wuhu River; it is a branch of the Great Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yeda—the state of Yeda—had its capital a little over two hundred li south of the Wuhu River and was a branch of the Great Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 勝兵者五六千人。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number five or six thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field five or six thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 俗善戰。

translations.literal: Their custom is skilled in warfare.
translations.idiomatic: They were skilled warriors.

sentences.zh: 先時國亂，突厥遣通設字詰強領其國。

translations.literal: Earlier the state fell into disorder, and the Turks dispatched a tongshe official, styled Jieqiang, to administer the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the kingdom had fallen into disorder, the Turks dispatched an official of tongshe rank, styled Jieqiang, to govern it.

sentences.zh: 都城方十餘里。

translations.literal: The capital city is a little over ten li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured a little over ten li square.

sentences.zh: 多寺塔，皆飾以金。

translations.literal: Monasteries and pagodas are many, all ornamented with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Monasteries and pagodas were numerous, all ornamented with gold.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同妻。

translations.literal: Brothers share one wife.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers shared a single wife.

sentences.zh: 婦人有一夫者，冠一角帽，夫兄弟多者，依其數為角。

translations.literal: A woman with one husband wears a single-horned cap; if her husband's brothers are many, the horns follow their number.
translations.idiomatic: A woman with one husband wore a single-horned cap; if her husbands were numerous among the brothers, the cap bore horns in corresponding number.

sentences.zh: 南去漕國千五百里，東去瓜州六千五百里。

translations.literal: South to Caoguo is one thousand five hundred li, east to Guazhou six thousand five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Kapiśa lay fifteen hundred li south, and Guazhou sixty-five hundred li east.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they sent envoys bearing local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it sent tribute missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 米國，都那密水西，舊康居之地也。

translations.literal: Mi—Mi State—has its capital west of the Namih River; it is the old land of Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Mi—the state of Mi—had its capital west of the Namih River, on former Kangju territory.

sentences.zh: 無王。

translations.literal: There is no king.
translations.idiomatic: It had no king of its own.

sentences.zh: 其城主姓昭武，康國王之支庶，字閉拙。

translations.literal: Its city lord's surname is Zhaowu, a cadet branch of the king of Kang; his style name is Bizhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Its city lord belonged to the Zhaowu clan, a cadet line of the king of Kang, and was styled Bizhuo.

sentences.zh: 都城方二里。

translations.literal: The capital city is two li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured two li square.

sentences.zh: 勝兵數百人。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field several hundred fighting men.

sentences.zh: 西北去康國百里，東去蘇對沙那國五百里，西南去史國二百里，東去瓜州六千四百里。

translations.literal: Northwest to Kang is one hundred li, east to Suduishana State five hundred li, southwest to Shi State two hundred li, east to Guazhou six thousand four hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Kang lay a hundred li northwest, Suduishana five hundred li east, Shi two hundred li southwest, and Guazhou sixty-four hundred li east.

sentences.zh: 大業中，頻貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they frequently sent local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it frequently sent local goods as tribute.

sentences.zh: 史國，都獨莫水南十里，舊康居之地也。

translations.literal: Shi—Shi State—has its capital ten li south of the Dumo River; it is the old land of Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Shi—the state of Shi—had its capital ten li south of the Dumo River, on former Kangju territory.

sentences.zh: 其王姓昭武，字逖遮，亦康國王之支庶也。

translations.literal: Its king's surname is Zhaowu; his style name is Tizhe; he too is a cadet branch of the king of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Zhaowu clan and was styled Tizhe, likewise a cadet branch of the king of Kang.

sentences.zh: 都城方二里。

translations.literal: The capital city is two li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured two li square.

sentences.zh: 勝兵千餘人。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number over one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field more than a thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 俗同康國。

translations.literal: Their customs are the same as Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs largely matched those of Kang.

sentences.zh: 北去康國二百四十里，南去吐火羅五百里，西去那色波國二百里，東北去米國二百里，東去瓜州六千五百里。

translations.literal: North to Kang is two hundred forty li, south to Tokhara five hundred li, west to Nasibo State two hundred li, northeast to Mi State two hundred li, east to Guazhou six thousand five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Kang lay two hundred forty li north, Tokhara five hundred li south, Nasibo two hundred li west, Mi two hundred li northeast, and Guazhou sixty-five hundred li east.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they sent envoys bearing local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it sent tribute missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 曹國，都那密水南數里，舊是康居之地也。

translations.literal: Cao—Cao State—has its capital several li south of the Namih River; it was formerly the land of Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Cao—the state of Cao—had its capital a few li south of the Namih River, on former Kangju territory.

sentences.zh: 國無主，康國王令子烏建領之。

translations.literal: The state has no ruler; the king of Kang ordered his son Wujian to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: The state had no ruler of its own; the king of Kang put his son Wujian in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 都城方三里。

translations.literal: The capital city is three li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured three li square.

sentences.zh: 勝兵千餘人。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number over one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field more than a thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 國中有得悉神，自西海以東諸國並敬事之。

translations.literal: Within the state there is the god Dexi; from the Western Sea eastward all states alike revere and serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Within the kingdom was the god Dexi, whom all states from the Western Sea eastward jointly revered.

sentences.zh: 其神有金人焉，金破羅闊丈有五尺，高下相稱。

translations.literal: This god has a golden image: a golden p'okara one zhang and five chi broad, proportioned in height and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: The deity had a golden image: a golden ritual vessel one zhang and five chi across, proportioned in height and breadth.

sentences.zh: 每日以駝五頭、馬十匹、羊一百口祭之，常有千人食之不盡。

translations.literal: Each day five camels, ten horses, and one hundred sheep are sacrificed to it; a thousand people regularly cannot finish eating the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Each day five camels, ten horses, and a hundred sheep were sacrificed to it, and a thousand people could not finish eating the offerings.

sentences.zh: 東南去康國百里，西去何國百五十里，東去瓜州六千六百里。

translations.literal: Southeast to Kang is one hundred li, west to He State one hundred fifty li, east to Guazhou six thousand six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Kang lay a hundred li southeast, He a hundred fifty li west, and Guazhou sixty-six hundred li east.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they sent envoys bearing local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it sent tribute missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 何國，都那密水南數里，舊是康居之地也。

translations.literal: He—He State—has its capital several li south of the Namih River; it was formerly the land of Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: He—the state of He—had its capital a few li south of the Namih River, on former Kangju territory.

sentences.zh: 其王姓昭武，亦康國王之族類，字敦。

translations.literal: Its king's surname is Zhaowu; he too is of the king of Kang's clan; his style name is Dun.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Zhaowu clan, kin to the ruler of Kang, and was styled Dun.

sentences.zh: 都城方二里。

translations.literal: The capital city is two li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured two li square.

sentences.zh: 勝兵千人。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field a thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 其王坐金羊座。

translations.literal: The king sits on a golden ram throne.
translations.idiomatic: The king sat upon a golden ram throne.

sentences.zh: 東去曹國百五十里，西去小安國三百里，東去瓜州六千七百五十里。

translations.literal: East to Cao State is one hundred fifty li, west to Lesser An State three hundred li, east to Guazhou six thousand seven hundred fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: Cao lay a hundred fifty li east, Lesser An three hundred li west, and Guazhou sixty-seven hundred fifty li east.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they sent envoys bearing local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it sent tribute missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 烏那曷國，都烏滸水西，舊安息之地也。

translations.literal: Wunahe—Wunahe State—has its capital west of the Wuhu River; it is the old land of Parthia.
translations.idiomatic: Wunahe—the state of Wunahe—had its capital west of the Wuhu River, on former Parthian territory.

sentences.zh: 王姓昭武，亦康國種類，字佛食。

translations.literal: The king's surname is Zhaowu; he is also of the Kang clan; his style name is Foshi.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Zhaowu clan, a branch kin to Kang, and was styled Foshi.

sentences.zh: 都城方二里。

translations.literal: The capital city is two li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured two li square.

sentences.zh: 勝兵數百人。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field several hundred fighting men.

sentences.zh: 王坐金羊座。

translations.literal: The king sits on a golden ram throne.
translations.idiomatic: The king sat upon a golden ram throne.

sentences.zh: 東北去安國四百里，西北去穆國二百餘里，東去瓜州七千五百里。

translations.literal: Northeast to An State is four hundred li, northwest to Mu State over two hundred li, east to Guazhou seven thousand five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: An lay four hundred li northeast, Mu over two hundred li northwest, and Guazhou seventy-five hundred li east.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they sent envoys bearing local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it sent tribute missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 穆國穆國，都烏滸河之西，亦安息之故地，與烏那曷為鄰。

translations.literal: Mu—Mu State—has its capital west of the Wuhu River; it is likewise the old land of Parthia and borders Wunahe.
translations.idiomatic: Mu—the state of Mu—had its capital west of the Wuhu River, likewise on former Parthian ground and bordering Wunahe.

sentences.zh: 其王姓昭武，亦康國王之種類也，字阿濫密。

translations.literal: Its king's surname is Zhaowu; he too is of the king of Kang's clan; his style name is Alanmi.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Zhaowu clan, likewise a branch of the ruler of Kang, and was styled Alanmi.

sentences.zh: 都城方三里。

translations.literal: The capital city is three li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured three li square.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二千人。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field two thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 東北去安國五百里，東去烏那曷二百餘里，西去波斯國四千餘里，東去瓜州七千七百里。

translations.literal: Northeast to An State is five hundred li, east to Wunahe over two hundred li, west to Persia over four thousand li, east to Guazhou seven thousand seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: An lay five hundred li northeast, Wunahe over two hundred li east, Persia over four thousand li west, and Guazhou seventy-seven hundred li east.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period, they sent envoys bearing local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era it sent tribute missions bearing local goods.

sentences.zh: 波斯波斯國，都達曷水之西蘇藺城即條支之故地也。

translations.literal: Persia—Persia State—has its capital at Sulon west of the Dahe River; it is the old land of Tiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Persia—the state of Persia—had its capital at Sulon west of the Dahe River, on the site known to the Han as Tiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 其王字庫薩和。

translations.literal: Its king's style name is Kusahe.
translations.idiomatic: The king was styled Kusahe.

sentences.zh: 都城方十餘里。

translations.literal: The capital city is a little over ten li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured a little over ten li square.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二萬餘人，乘象而戰。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number over twenty thousand men; they ride elephants in battle.
translations.idiomatic: It could field more than twenty thousand fighting men and went to war mounted on elephants.

sentences.zh: 國無死刑，或斷手刖足，沒家財，或剃去其鬚，或繫排於項，以為標異。

translations.literal: The state has no death penalty; some have hands cut off or feet amputated and household goods confiscated, some have their beards shaved off, or wooden placards are tied at the neck as marks of disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom had no death penalty; offenders might have hands or feet severed and their household goods confiscated, their beards shaved off, or wooden placards hung from the neck as marks of disgrace.

sentences.zh: 人年三歲已上，出口錢四文。

translations.literal: For people three years of age and above, an exit tax of four cash is levied.
translations.idiomatic: Every person from the age of three upward paid an exit tax of four cash.

sentences.zh: 妻其姊妹。

translations.literal: Men marry their sisters.
translations.idiomatic: Men married their sisters.

sentences.zh: 人死者，棄屍于山，持服一月。

translations.literal: When a person dies, the corpse is abandoned on a mountain; mourning dress is worn for one month.
translations.idiomatic: When someone died the body was abandoned on a mountain, and mourners wore mourning dress for one month.

sentences.zh: 王著金花冠，坐金師子座，傅金屑於鬚上以為飾。

translations.literal: The king wears a golden-flower crown, sits on a golden lion throne, and applies gold dust to his beard as ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a golden-flower crown, sat upon a golden lion throne, and dusted gold powder into his beard as ornament.

sentences.zh: 衣錦袍，加瓔珞於其上。

translations.literal: He wears a brocade robe, with jeweled chains added upon it.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a brocade robe with jeweled chains added over it.

sentences.zh: 土多良馬，大驢，師子，白象，大鳥卵，真珠，頗黎，獸魄，珊瑚，瑠璃，碼碯，水精，瑟瑟，呼洛羯，呂騰，火齊，金剛，金，銀，鍮石，銅，鑌鐵，錫，錦疊，細布，氍㲣，毾㲪，護那，越諾布，檀，金縷織成，赤麖皮，朱沙，水銀，薰陸、鬱金、蘇合、青木等諸香，胡椒，畢撥，石蜜，半蜜，千年棗，附子，訶黎勒，無食子，鹽綠，雌黃。

translations.literal: The soil has many fine horses, large donkeys, lions, white elephants, large bird eggs, pearls, boli glass, amber, coral, lapis lazuli, agate, crystal, sese stones, huluojie, lüteng, fire-qi gems, diamonds, gold, silver, orpiment, copper, patterned steel, tin, layered brocade, fine cloth, qulu carpets, ta carpets, huna cloth, yuenuo cloth, sandalwood, gold-thread woven fabric, red musk-deer hide, cinnabar, mercury, frankincense, turmeric, storax, lign aloes, and other incenses, pepper, long pepper, rock candy, half-honey, thousand-year jujubes, aconite, haritaki, myrobalan galls, green salt, and orpiment.
translations.idiomatic: The land abounded in fine horses, large donkeys, lions, white elephants, ostrich eggs, pearls, crystal, amber, coral, lapis lazuli, agate, rock crystal, turquoise sese stones, huluojie and lüteng textiles, carnelian, diamonds, gold, silver, orpiment, copper, patterned steel, tin, layered brocades, fine cloth, qulu and ta carpets, huna and yuenuo fabrics, sandalwood, gold-thread weaving, red musk-deer hides, cinnabar, mercury, frankincense, turmeric, storax, lign aloes, and other aromatics, pepper, long pepper, rock candy, half-refined honey, thousand-year jujubes, aconite, haritaki, myrobalan galls, green salt, and realgar.

sentences.zh: 突厥不能至其國，亦羈縻之。

translations.literal: The Turks cannot reach this state, yet it too is held loosely in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Turks could not reach this kingdom, yet it too was held only loosely within the tributary orbit.

sentences.zh: 波斯每遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: Persia repeatedly sends envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Persia sent tribute missions repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 西去海數百里，東去穆國四千餘里，西北去拂菻四千五百里，東去瓜州萬一千七百里。

translations.literal: West to the sea is several hundred li, east to Mu State over four thousand li, northwest to Fulin four thousand five hundred li, east to Guazhou eleven thousand seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The sea lay several hundred li west, Mu over four thousand li east, Fulin forty-five hundred li northwest, and Guazhou eleven thousand seven hundred li east.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣雲騎尉李昱使通波斯，尋遣使隨昱貢方物。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang dispatched Cloud-Cavalry Commandant Li Yu as envoy to open relations with Persia; soon afterward envoys followed Li Yu bearing local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang dispatched Cloud-Cavalry Commandant Li Yu to open relations with Persia, and soon afterward the Persians sent envoys with Li Yu bearing local goods in tribute.

sentences.zh: 漕國，在葱嶺之北，漢時𦋺賓國也。

translations.literal: Caoguo—Caoguo State—lies north of the Pamirs; in Han times it was the state of Kapiśa.
translations.idiomatic: Caoguo—the state of Caoguo—lay north of the Pamirs and was the Han-era kingdom of Kapiśa.

sentences.zh: 其王姓昭武，字順達，康國王之宗族。

translations.literal: Its king's surname is Zhaowu; his style name is Shunda; he is of the king of Kang's clan.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Zhaowu clan and was styled Shunda, of the royal kindred of Kang.

sentences.zh: 都城方四里。

translations.literal: The capital city is four li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured four li square.

sentences.zh: 勝兵者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Battle-ready troops number over ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field more than ten thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 國法嚴整，殺人及賊盜皆死。

translations.literal: The state's laws are strict and orderly; murder and theft are all punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: Its laws were stern: murder and theft were capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 其俗淫祠。

translations.literal: Their custom is lavish cult worship.
translations.idiomatic: Their cultic practice was lavish and licentious.

sentences.zh: 葱嶺山有順天神者，儀制極華，金銀鍱為屋，以銀為地，祠者日有千餘人。

translations.literal: On Mount Pamir there is the god Shuntian, whose ritual regalia is extremely splendid: gold and silver sheets form the house, silver serves as the floor, and worshippers number over one thousand daily.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Pamir stood the god Shuntian, whose cult was magnificently appointed: the shrine was built of sheets of gold and silver with a silver floor, and more than a thousand worshippers came daily.

sentences.zh: 祠前有一魚脊骨，其孔中通，馬騎出入。

translations.literal: Before the shrine is a fish spine whose hollow passage runs through; mounted riders pass in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Before the shrine lay a fish spine whose hollow passage was wide enough for a mounted rider to pass through.

sentences.zh: 國王戴金魚頭冠，坐金馬座。

translations.literal: The king wears a golden fish-head crown and sits on a golden horse throne.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a golden fish-head crown and sat upon a golden horse throne.

sentences.zh: 土多稻、粟、豆、麥；

translations.literal: The soil has much rice, millet, beans, and wheat;
translations.idiomatic: The land produced rice, millet, beans, and wheat;

sentences.zh: 饒象，馬，封牛，金，銀，鑌鐵，氍㲣，朱砂，青黛，安息、青木等香，石蜜，半蜜，黑鹽，阿魏，沒藥，白附子。

translations.literal: Elephants are abundant, together with horses, humped cattle, gold, silver, patterned steel, qulu carpets, cinnabar, indigo, Parthian and lign aloes incenses, rock candy, half-honey, black salt, asafetida, myrrh, and white aconite.
translations.idiomatic: elephants were plentiful, along with horses, humped cattle, gold, silver, patterned steel, qulu carpets, cinnabar, indigo, Parthian and lign aloes aromatics, rock candy, half-refined honey, black salt, asafetida, myrrh, and white aconite.

sentences.zh: 北去帆延七百里，東去刦國六百里，東北去瓜州六千六百里。

translations.literal: North to Fanyan is seven hundred li, east to Jie State six hundred li, northeast to Guazhou six thousand six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Fanyan lay seven hundred li north, Jie six hundred li east, and Guazhou sixty-six hundred li northeast.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, they sent envoys presenting local products in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign, Caoguo sent envoys bearing local goods in tribute.

sentences.zh: 附國附國者，蜀郡西北二千餘里，即漢之西南夷也。

translations.literal: Fu Kingdom—Fu Kingdom—lies more than two thousand li northwest of Shu commandery; it is the Southwest Yi of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Fu—called Fu Kingdom—lay more than two thousand li northwest of Shu commandery; in Han times it had been one of the Southwest Yi peoples.

sentences.zh: 有嘉良夷，即其東部，所居種姓自相率領，土俗與附國同，言語少殊，不相統一。

translations.literal: There are the Jialiang Yi, that is its eastern part; the clans dwelling there lead themselves, local customs are the same as Fu Kingdom, language slightly different, not unified under one rule.
translations.idiomatic: The Jialiang Yi occupied its eastern regions. Local clans lived under their own leaders, their customs matched those of Fu, though their speech differed slightly, and they were not united under a single authority.

sentences.zh: 其人並無姓氏。

translations.literal: These people all have no surnames.
translations.idiomatic: None of them used surnames.

sentences.zh: 附國王字宜繒。

translations.literal: The king of Fu Kingdom's style name is Yizeng.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Fu was styled Yizeng.

sentences.zh: 其國南北八百里，東南千五百里，無城柵，近川谷，傍山險。

translations.literal: Its state is eight hundred li north-south, one thousand five hundred li southeast, has no walls or palisades, lies near river valleys, adjoining perilous mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom measured eight hundred li north to south and fifteen hundred li east to southeast. It had no walled towns or stockades; settlements lay along river valleys against steep mountain slopes.

sentences.zh: 俗好復讎，故壘石為𥕘而居，以避其患。

translations.literal: Custom favors taking revenge, therefore they pile stones into tower-dwellings to live in, to avoid this trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Because blood feuds were common, they built stone tower-dwellings to live in and escape that danger.

sentences.zh: 其𥕘高至十餘丈，下至五六丈，每級丈餘，以木隔之。

translations.literal: These towers reach heights of more than ten zhang at the top, down to five or six zhang at the bottom, each tier more than one zhang, separated by wood.
translations.idiomatic: The towers stood anywhere from five or six to more than ten zhang high, each tier rising over a zhang with wooden floors between levels.

sentences.zh: 基方三四步，𥕘上方二三步，狀似浮圖。

translations.literal: The base is three or four paces square, the top of the tower two or three paces, shaped like a pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: Each stood on a base three or four paces square, narrowed to two or three paces at the top, and looked like a pagoda.

sentences.zh: 於下級開小門，從內上通，夜必關閉，以防賊盜。

translations.literal: On the lower tier a small door is opened, passage upward from within; at night it must be closed shut, to guard against thieves and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: A small door opened at the lowest level gave internal access upward; it was always bolted at night against thieves.

sentences.zh: 國有二萬餘家，號令自王出。

translations.literal: The state has more than twenty thousand households; orders and decrees issue from the king.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom contained more than twenty thousand households, and all government orders came from the king.

sentences.zh: 嘉良夷政令繫之酋帥，重罪者死，輕刑罰牛。

translations.literal: The Jialiang Yi's government and laws depend on their chieftains; serious crimes are punished by death, light punishments by fining cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Jialiang Yi, each chieftain enforced the law locally: capital crimes merited death, lesser offenses were punished with fines paid in cattle.

sentences.zh: 人皆輕捷，便於擊劍。

translations.literal: The people are all light and nimble, skilled at sword combat.
translations.idiomatic: The people were agile and skilled swordsmen.

sentences.zh: 漆皮為牟甲，弓長六尺，以竹為弦。

translations.literal: Lacquered hide serves as armor, bows are six chi long, bamboo serves as the string.
translations.idiomatic: They wore lacquered leather armor; their bows were six chi long with bamboo strings.

sentences.zh: 妻其羣母及嫂，兒弟死，父兄亦納其妻。

translations.literal: They take as wives their stepmothers and sisters-in-law; when younger brothers die, fathers and elder brothers also take in their wives.
translations.idiomatic: A man might marry his stepmothers and sisters-in-law; when a younger brother died, his father or elder brothers would take the widow.

sentences.zh: 好歌儛，鼓簧，吹長笛。

translations.literal: They love song and dance, beating the reed pipe, blowing the long flute.
translations.idiomatic: They loved song and dance, playing reed pipes and long flutes.

sentences.zh: 有死者，無服制，置屍高牀之上，沐浴衣服，被以牟甲，覆以獸皮。

translations.literal: When there is a death, there is no mourning dress code; the corpse is placed on a high bed, bathed and clothed, covered with armor, overlaid with animal hides.
translations.idiomatic: When someone died, no mourning garb was prescribed. The body was laid on a high platform, washed and dressed, clad in armor, and covered with animal hides.

sentences.zh: 子孫不哭，帶甲儛劍而呼云：「我父為鬼所取，我欲報冤殺鬼。」

translations.literal: The sons and grandsons do not weep; wearing armor, dancing with swords, they cry out saying: "My father was taken by a ghost; I wish to avenge the wrong and kill the ghost.
translations.idiomatic: The sons and grandsons did not weep. Instead they donned armor, danced with swords drawn, and shouted: "My father was seized by a ghost—I will avenge him and slay the ghost!

sentences.zh: 自餘親戚哭三聲而止。

translations.literal: The remaining relatives weep three cries and stop.
translations.idiomatic: Other relatives cried out three times and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 婦人哭，必以兩手掩面。

translations.literal: When women weep, they must cover their faces with both hands.
translations.idiomatic: Women mourners always covered their faces with both hands.

sentences.zh: 死家殺牛，親屬以猪酒相遺，共飲噉而瘞之。

translations.literal: The dead person's family slaughters an ox; relatives send one another pork and wine, jointly eating and drinking and then burying him.
translations.idiomatic: The bereaved family slaughtered an ox; relatives exchanged gifts of pork and wine, feasted together, and then buried the body.

sentences.zh: 死後十年而大葬，其葬必集親賓，殺馬動至數十匹。

translations.literal: Ten years after death comes the great burial; the burial always gathers kin and guests, slaughtering horses often reaching several tens of head.
translations.idiomatic: A great funeral was held ten years after death, attended by kin and guests; dozens of horses might be slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 立其祖父神而事之。

translations.literal: They erect the spirits of their fathers and grandfathers and serve them.
translations.idiomatic: They set up ancestral spirits of fathers and grandfathers and worshipped them.

sentences.zh: 其俗以皮為帽，形圓如鉢，或帶羃䍦。

translations.literal: Their custom uses hide for hats, round in shape like a bowl, or they wear face veils.
translations.idiomatic: They wore round leather caps shaped like bowls, or face veils.

sentences.zh: 衣多毛毼皮裘，全剝牛脚皮為靴。

translations.literal: Clothing is mostly felted wool or fur coats; they fully peel cattle hoof skin to make boots.
translations.idiomatic: Their clothing was chiefly felted wool and fur; boots were made entirely from the skin of cattle hooves.

sentences.zh: 項繫鐵鎖，手貫鐵釧。

translations.literal: On the neck they wear iron chains; on the hands iron bangles.
translations.idiomatic: They wore iron chains around the neck and iron bangles on the wrists.

sentences.zh: 王與酋帥，金為首飾，胸前懸一金花，徑三寸。

translations.literal: The king and chieftains use gold for head ornaments; a golden flower hangs before the chest, three cun in diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Kings and chieftains wore gold head ornaments and hung a golden flower three cun across on the chest.

sentences.zh: 其土高，氣候涼，多風少雨。

translations.literal: Its land is high, the climate cool, much wind and little rain.
translations.idiomatic: The land was high and the climate cool, with frequent winds and scant rain.

sentences.zh: 土宜小麥、青𮃡。

translations.literal: The soil suits wheat and highland barley.
translations.idiomatic: The soil favored wheat and highland barley.

sentences.zh: 山出金、銀、多白雉。

translations.literal: The mountains produce gold and silver; white pheasants are numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains yielded gold and silver, and white pheasants were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 水有嘉魚，長四尺而鱗細。

translations.literal: The waters have fine fish, four chi long with fine scales.
translations.idiomatic: The rivers held splendid fish four chi long with fine scales.

sentences.zh: 大業四年，其王遣使素福等八人入朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daye, its king sent eight envoys including Sufu to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daye, the king sent eight envoys led by Sufu to the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 明年，又遣其弟子宜林率嘉良夷六十人朝貢。

translations.literal: The next year, he again sent his younger kinsman Yilin leading sixty Jialiang Yi to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sent his young kinsman Yilin at the head of sixty Jialiang Yi to pay tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 欲獻良馬，以路險不通，請開山道以修職貢。

translations.literal: Wishing to present fine horses, because the roads were perilous and impassable, they requested that a mountain route be opened to maintain tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: They wished to offer fine horses but the route was too dangerous; they asked that a mountain road be cut so they could fulfill their tribute obligations.

sentences.zh: 煬帝以勞人不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang, on grounds of burdening the people, did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang refused, unwilling to burden the populace with such labor.

sentences.zh: 嘉良有水，闊六七十丈，附國有水，闊百餘丈，並南流，用皮為舟而濟。

translations.literal: Jialiang has a river, sixty or seventy zhang wide; Fu Kingdom has a river, over one hundred zhang wide; both flow south; they use hide boats to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Jialiang had a river sixty or seventy zhang wide; Fu had one over a hundred zhang wide. Both flowed south, and people crossed in boats made of hides.

sentences.zh: 附國南有薄緣夷，風俗亦同。

translations.literal: South of Fu Kingdom are the Boyuan Yi, customs also the same.
translations.idiomatic: South of Fu lived the Boyuan Yi, whose customs were much the same.

sentences.zh: 西有女國。

translations.literal: To the west is the Women's Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: To the west lay the Women's Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 其東北連山，緜亘數千里，接於党項。

translations.literal: Its northeast has connected mountains, stretching continuously for several thousand li, joining with the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast, mountains ran unbroken for thousands of li, reaching the Tangut lands.

sentences.zh: 往往有羌：大、小左封，昔衞，葛延，白狗，向人，望族，林臺，春桑，利豆，迷桑，婢藥，大硤，白蘭，叱利摸徒，那鄂，當迷，渠步，桑悟，千碉，並在深山窮谷，無大君長。

translations.literal: Here and there are Qiang: Great and Lesser Zuofeng, Xiewei, Geyan, Baigou, Xiangren, Wangzu, Lintai, Chunsang, Lidou, Misang, Biyao, Daxia, Bailan, Chilimotu, Na'e, Dangmi, Qubu, Sangwu, Qiandiao—all in deep mountains and remote valleys, with no great rulers or chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered Qiang groups were found throughout the region—the Great and Lesser Zuofeng, Xiewei, Geyan, Baigou, Xiangren, Wangzu, Lintai, Chunsang, Lidou, Misang, Biyao, Daxia, Bailan, Chilimotu, Na'e, Dangmi, Qubu, Sangwu, and Qiandiao—all dwelling in deep mountains and remote valleys without any paramount chief.

sentences.zh: 其風俗略同於党項，或役屬吐谷渾，或附附國。

translations.literal: Their customs are roughly the same as the Tangut; some are subject to the Tuyuhun, some attached to Fu Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs broadly resembled those of the Tangut; some served the Tuyuhun, others were attached to Fu.

sentences.zh: 大業中，來朝貢。

translations.literal: During the Daye era, they came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign they came to court bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 緣西南邊置諸道總管，以遙管之。

translations.literal: Along the southwestern frontier various circuit administrators-general were installed to govern them from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The court placed circuit administrators-general along the southwestern frontier to oversee them at a distance.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自古開遠夷，通絕域，必因宏放之主，皆起好事之臣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: From antiquity, opening distant Yi and connecting with cut-off regions has always depended on broad-minded sovereigns, all arising from ministers who loved grand projects.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: Since antiquity, reaching distant barbarians and opening routes to the farthest lands has always required a magnanimous ruler—and has always been set in motion by ministers eager for bold undertakings.

sentences.zh: 張騫鑿空於前，班超投筆於後，或結之以重寶，或懾之以利劍，投軀萬死之地，以要一旦之功，皆由主尚來遠之名，臣殉輕生之節。

translations.literal: Zhang Qian opened the void in front, Ban Chao threw aside his brush behind; some were bound with heavy treasure, some intimidated with sharp swords; they cast their bodies into lands of ten thousand deaths to seize a moment's achievement—all because the ruler valued the fame of drawing the distant, and ministers martyred themselves to the virtue of treating life lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian had pioneered the route in the Han, Ban Chao had cast aside his writing brush to follow—some were won with lavish gifts, others cowed with drawn swords. Men threw themselves into mortal danger for a single burst of glory, all because the sovereign coveted renown from afar and his servants were ready to squander their lives for the cause.

sentences.zh: 是知上之所好，下必有甚者也。

translations.literal: From this one knows: what those above favor, those below will surely exceed.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that whatever the ruler favors, his subjects will pursue with even greater zeal.

sentences.zh: 煬帝規摹宏侈，掩吞秦、漢，裴矩方進西域圖記以蕩其心，故萬乘親出玉門關，置伊吾、且末，而關右暨於流沙，騷然無聊生矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang's plans and models were grand and extravagant, swallowing Qin and Han; Pei Ju had just presented his Western Regions map-chronicle to shake his heart, therefore the ten-thousand-chariot sovereign personally went out through Yumen Pass, established Yiwu and Qiemo, and the lands west of the passes reaching to the shifting sands were in uproar with no means of living peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang's ambitions were vast enough to overshadow Qin and Han combined. Pei Ju had just submitted his Western Regions gazetteer to inflame those ambitions, so the Son of Heaven himself marched beyond Yumen Pass, established garrisons at Yiwu and Qiemo, and the regions west of the passes as far as the shifting sands were thrown into such turmoil that ordinary people could scarcely live.

sentences.zh: 若使北狄無虞，東夷告捷，必將修輪臺之戍，築烏壘之城，求大秦之明珠，致條支之鳥卵，往來轉輸，將何以堪其敝哉！

translations.literal: If the northern Di gave no trouble and the eastern Yi reported victory, they would surely restore the garrison at Luntai, build the fortress at Wulei, seek the bright pearls of Daqin, procure the birds' eggs of Tiaozhi—how could the back-and-forth transport bear such exhaustion!
translations.idiomatic: Had the northern barbarians stayed quiet and the eastern tribes brought good news, the court would inevitably have restored the Luntai garrison, rebuilt Wulei fortress, demanded the luminous pearls of Rome, and fetched the ostrich eggs of Tiaozhi—with goods shuttling ceaselessly back and forth, how could the empire have endured the strain?

sentences.zh: 古者哲王之制，方五千里，務安諸夏，不事要荒。

translations.literal: In antiquity the wise kings' institutions extended five thousand li square, striving to settle the various Xia, not serving the distant wastes.
translations.idiomatic: The institutions of the sage kings of old measured five thousand li square; their aim was to secure the Central States, not to meddle in the far wastes.

sentences.zh: 豈威不能加，德不能被？

translations.literal: Could their authority not reach there, their virtue not cover it?
translations.idiomatic: Was it that their power could not reach so far, or their virtue could not extend there?

sentences.zh: 蓋不以四夷勞中國，不以無用害有用也。

translations.literal: It is rather that they did not use the Four Yi to exhaust the Middle Kingdom, did not let the useless harm the useful.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, they refused to exhaust the Central Kingdom for the sake of the four barbarian quarters, or to sacrifice what was useful for what was worthless.

sentences.zh: 是以秦戍五嶺，漢事三邊，或道殣相望，或戶口減半。

translations.literal: Therefore Qin garrisoned the Five Ridges, Han handled the three frontiers—sometimes corpses lined the roads, sometimes household registers were halved.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Qin posted troops to the Five Ridges and Han poured resources into the three frontiers—with corpses sometimes lining the roads and registered populations cut in half.

sentences.zh: 隋室恃其強盛，亦狼狽於青海。

translations.literal: The Sui house, relying on its strength and prosperity, also ended up in disarray at Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui dynasty, confident in its strength, likewise found itself in desperate straits on the Qinghai frontier.

sentences.zh: 此皆一人失其道，故億兆罹其毒。

translations.literal: All this because one man lost the Way, therefore the hundred millions suffered its poison.
translations.idiomatic: All of this stemmed from one man's loss of the Way—and hundreds of millions bore the cost.

sentences.zh: 若深思即叙之義，固辭都護之請，返其千里之馬，不求白狼之貢，則七戎九夷，候風重譯，雖無遼東之捷，豈及江都之禍乎！

translations.literal: If one deeply contemplated the meaning of immediate compliance and order, firmly declined requests for protectorates, returned their thousand-li horses, did not seek the tribute of the white wolf, then the seven Rong and nine Yi, waiting for the wind and passing through repeated translations, though without victory in Liaodong—how could they have reached the disaster of Jiangdu!
translations.idiomatic: Had the emperor truly grasped the principle of ruling distant peoples through peaceful submission—firmly declining requests for protectorates, sending back horses offered from a thousand li away, and spurning exotic tribute like the white wolf's pelt—then the peoples of west and east would still have come bearing gifts through interpreters, wind at their backs. The court might have won no triumph in Liaodong, but would it ever have suffered catastrophe at Jiangdu?
